It’s a critical game for both teams. The Packers remain in last place in the NFC North, even while winning five of their last six games. The Vikings have lost two consecutive games following a 6-0 start. Who will win the game? And, with this being the halfway point of the season, who will lead the team in rushing, receiving and sacks? And, ultimately, what will be the team’s final record and playoff fate? Here are our Packers-Vikings picks and midseason predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Vikings Prediction The Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins this week. It’s a huge move for the Vikings, who somehow are 6-2 despite their quarterbacks’ inability to get the ball to Justin Jefferson. Cousins has faced the Packers 10 times while with the Vikings. He topped a 110 passer rating in seven of those games. OK, but what about this season? With the Raiders, Cousins ranked fifth in passing yards, second in touchdown passes and 11th in passer rating. Plain and simple, he remains a quality starting quarterback. Maybe I’m guilty of overvaluing Cousins. Maybe I’m undervaluing Jordan Love’s ability to consistently make plays against a Vikings defense that has won every matchup this season. Ultimately, I think Cousins will make one more big play, Love will be forced into one more big mistake and the special teams will get in the way. Score: Vikings 20, Packers 17 Bill’s Record: 7-2. Jacob Westendorf’s Packers-Vikings Prediction Yes, Kirk Cousins is back, but Green Bay's defense is for real until proven otherwise. The Packers had some answers for Brian Flores' group in Week 1 until Jordan Love was snowed under by Minnesota's pressure. This time, Lambeau Field will be the X-factor as the offensive line will be able to hear Love manipulate the line of scrimmage, which will help him make one more play than Cousins, as the Packers score a big win heading into their bye week. Score: Packers 21, Vikings 17. Jacob’s Record: 6-3. Jacob: Second (Chicago wins the NFC North thanks to a win on Christmas Day at Soldier Field). Who Will Lead Packers in Sacks? Bill: Lukas Van Ness. I came up with this question in light of Micah Parsons’ presumptive return for the game against the Rams. Tucker Kraft has had a quiet season following last year’s torn ACL. It’s just part of coming off a major injury. So, while I thought about going with Parsons here, Van Ness will maintain the team lead and finish with eight sacks. Jacob: Lukas Van Ness. Van Ness has 4.5 sacks, which leads the team. His job should get a little easier with Micah Parsons' return to the lineup as he'll see less double teams. Parsons is a good bet here, as well, but has noted it may take him a while to look like himself again. The goal for the Packers is going to be to have him at his best in the postseason. The guess here is that he's out of Matt LaFleur's doghouse and going to be a more focal point of Green Bay's offense in Josh Jacobs' absence. The sheer volume of passes going to Golden will push him past the explosive play off Watson, especially if last week’s game signals that his drops are behind him. The big question: Can they set the combined yardage record? Jacob: Christian Watson. This might be one of the most intriguing storylines down the stretch. Watson and Golden are neck and neck in this category now, with Watson holding a slight advantage. Watson is used to playing this late in the season and has made some big plays in big games. Golden has, as well, so this will be really close as the season comes to a close, but give us Watson to go over 1,200 yards for the season and earn the team's receiving title. Will Jordan Love Lead NFL in Passing Yards? Bill: Entering Sunday, Cincinnati’s Joe Burrow leads the NFL with 298.3 passing yards per game. Jordan Love is hot on his heels with a 290.9-yard average. That’s less than a first down per game. Playing five consecutive cold-weather games down the stretch isn’t going to help Love in his pursuit. Jacob: Yes, the only way the Packers can move the ball is on the right arm of Jordan Love. There's little reason to believe that's going to change, even when the elements start turning colder. Add in some games that could be potential shootouts, like a home game against Buffalo or a road game against Chicago. That could cause Love to pile up some big numbers. How Will the Season End? Bill: With the entire NFC North earning their way into the playoff field, the last-place Packers will squeak into the postseason as the No. 7 seed. It’s obviously a familiar place for the Packers. And it’s a death sentence. The No. 7 seed has to play at the No. 2 seed. If the No. 7 pulls off an upset, it will have to play at the No. 1 seed. So, let’s roll with the Packers upsetting the rival Bears in the wild-card round but meeting their maker against the playoff-rival 49ers in the divisional round. Jacob: The Packers will earn the NFC's fifth seed and have a date with the NFC South-winning Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the first round of the playoffs. A big game from Jordan Love and Christian Watson, coupled with a suffocating defensive performance in which Micah Parsons will collect three sacks and a forced fumble against Baker Mayfield, will give the team its first playoff win since 2023. They will follow that by avenging last year's loss in the playoffs to the Chicago Bears by knocking them out at Soldier Field in the divisional round on a game-winning field goal from Trey Smack. That sends them to San Francisco, a house of horrors, for the NFC Championship Game, where the season ultimately will end with Brock Purdy leading a late touchdown drive to send the Packers into an offseason short of the Super Bowl. No team has ever blitzed as much as this year's Vikings, and they have blitzed Packers QB Jordan Love with even greater frequency. away.headline: Packers appear built to withstand key injuries vs. Vikings in Week 10
away.blurb: The Green Bay Packers are set to face the Minnesota Vikings in a game they must win to remain in the thick of the NFC North race . At 6-3, the Packers could move ahead of Minnesota in the division rankings if they come out on top. The Packers listed Xavier McKinney and Kevin Zeitler as questionable The Packers posted their final injury report for Week 10. Offensive guard Kevin Zeitler (ankle/triceps), safety Xavier McKinney (foot), edge rusher Lukas Van Ness (back), Javon Bullard (ankle/knee), wide receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), and running back Chris Moore (ankle) had the questionable designation. Now, just because they popped up on the injury report doesn't mean that they won't be available against the Vikings. That said, not having McKinney would be a huge blow. If the All-Pro safety isn't good to go, Kitan Oladapo may get the starting nod next to Evan Williams. However, the task became substantially tougher when the Vikes traded for Kirk Cousins. Compounding the issue is that Green Bay could be without a handful of key players. Oladapo logged 14 defensive snaps in the win over the New England Patriots when Evan Williams briefly left the bout . He has played a total of 28 snaps at safety that year, so you can bet Kirk Cousins could try to target him. The silver lining is that defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon has done a good job of game-planning for Kirk throughout his coaching career , so he should have a trick or two prepared to stop the Minnesota offense. On the other hand, Green Bay should be able to withstand Zeitler's absence if he isn't good to go. If the veteran hog molly doesn't suit up, the Packers can easily plug in Laken Tomlinson at right guard and Aaron Banks on the left side. Granted, that's the lineup they've employed the past two games. Then again, the expectation was that after Zeitler made his debut against New England, he would see an uptick in playing time and possibly start at right guard. However, it looks like the coaching staff will have to halt the plan, as injuries have prevented him from hitting his stride since landing in Titletown in late September. Jordan Love gives the Packers the best chance to beat the VIkings Whether Kevin Zeitler starts or not, the Green Bay offensive line will be in good shape in Week 10. And that's the thing, if the Packers want to have a shot at beating Minnesota, they will need to keep Jordan Love upright. The Vikes have the top-ranked defense in the NFL. Sure, their run defense is 22nd in yards allowed, but can you truly trust Green Bay's underwhelming rushing attack to move the football? That means that it will be up to Love to put the team on his shoulders, and having a clean pocket will most definitely help. If defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon and his unit, with or without Xavier McKinney, can generate enough stops and give the offense a couple extra possessions, the Packers should be able to earn their seventh win of the season. away.headline: Kyler Murray Injury Update, New NFL Rumors on Vikings QB's Return Timeline After Kirk Cousins Trade
away.blurb: The 29-year-old quarterback could be targeting Minnesota's Week 12 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons for his potential return, according to Pelissero. Bleacher Report • 7h Oklahoma Calls Out SEC 😬 Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray is still "a couple of weeks away" from returning from his Grade 2 hamstring strain, NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported on Saturday. Murray's absence doesn't seem as urgent after the Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders in exchange for a third-round draft pick. If Cousins misses time, the team will have to turn to Carson Wentz, who is serving as the backup in Murray's absence. Mac Jones' Price too High for Vikings Murray suffered the injury during a 19-15 loss against the Detroit Lions in Week 8. He also missed Week 2 after suffering a concussion in Minnesota's regular-season opener. Although Murray compiled a 5-1 record as a starter this season, he was at the helm of a struggling Vikings offense. The eighth-year quarterback has just 1,022 passing yards with five touchdowns and three interceptions. Wentz struggled mightily when he stepped in for Murray on Monday night against the Buffalo Bills. He completed just 32 percent of his passes for 81 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions. Minnesota showed interest in reuniting with Cousins prior to Monday night , but Wentz' poor performance likely made it easier for the Vikings to name Cousins as the starter for a pivotal matchup against the Green Bay Packers in Week 10. Cousins is already familiar with head coach Kevin O'Connell's offensive system from the last two seasons of his six-year stint in Minnesota. He also has plenty of chemistry with star wide receiver Justin Jefferson, who enjoyed his most productive years on the receiving end of Cousins' passes. Cousins and O'Connell both struggled after parting ways, but they now have an opportunity to make up for lost time. Still, Murray's availability could prove valuable behind a 38-year-old quarterback. home.headline: NFL insider reveals Josh Jacobs injury return timeline for Packers after surgery
home.blurb: Green Bay Packers star running back Josh Jacobs suffered a fractured ring finger on his right hand during his team’s 45-27 beatdown of the New England Patriots this past weekend, leaving his availability in question. The injury required surgery, and now an update has emerged on Jacobs’ potential return for the Packers. According to Netflix NFL insider Tom Pelissero , Jacobs underwent successful surgery on his fractured ring finger on Friday in Los Angeles, with noted hand and wrist surgeon Dr. Steven Shin performing the procedure. Pelissero reported that Jacobs is expected to return to the Packers in the “next several weeks.” What George Pickens’ Bizarre Answer Means for His Cowboys Return vs. 49ers That could bode well for a Packers team that has won its last two games to improve to 6-3 this season in the competitive NFC North. Jacobs missed six games after being placed on the Commissioner’s Exempt List amid a domestic dispute and the NFL reinstated Jacobs last month. However, his three games since returning haven’t been as productive as he or the team may have hoped. Jacobs recorded 36 carries for just 80 yards and one touchdown before suffering his finger injury against New England. More news: Lions HC Dan Campbell Reveals Major Drake Maye Concern Before Patriots Clash He’s been a key offensive component for the Packers for the past two seasons. He had 1,329 yards and 15 touchdowns in his debut season for Green Bay, and then 929 rushing yards and 13 touchdowns last season. With Jacobs sidelined for the next several weeks, Kaleb Johnson could now take on a bigger workload for the Packers. Johnson has appeared in seven games, tallying 42 carries for 172 yards and one touchdown. MarShawn Lloyd has played in eight games for the Packers and has 149 rushing yards with two touchdowns to give Green Bay additional options at the position. Green Bay is heading into a challenging matchup this Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings, considered one of the league’s top defenses. The Packers’ running game could be important in taking pressure off quarterback Jordan Love. The Vikings also just added quarterback Kirk Cousins ahead of Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, potentially providing a significant upgrade for a struggling offense in the competitive NFC North. The Green Bay Packers face the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 15, beginning at 1 p.m. ET. picks.blurb: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars vs. Titans: Which New Addition Makes the First Big Play Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- After a frantic start to the week that saw the Jacksonville Jaguars make the biggest moves of this year's NFL Trade Deadline, it is worth remember that the Jaguars do, in fact, have an opponent on Sunday. The 6-2 Jaguars are set to travel to Nissan Stadium to face the Tennessee Titans in Week 10, their first game since making blockbuster trades for Jessie Bates and Jordan Davis, along with adding Davon Godchaux for a sixth-round pick. For a Jaguars team that has their eyes set on an AFC South title and a top seed in the playoffs, they are treating the Titans with the same seriousness that they treated the Indianapolis Colts and Baltimore Ravens over the last two weeks. So, how do we see the Jaguars' Week 10 battle with the Titans playing out? We break it down below. Jessie Bates Records An Interception While it certainly remains to be seen if the Jaguars will actually play any of their new defensive pieces against the Titans, I believe they will. Jakobi Meyers and Greg Newsome each played in their first games with the franchise last season after joining the team during that same week, and I think that means we see the trio make their Jaguars debuts. In the process, I think we see Bates create his first Jaguars takeaway right off the bat. Cam Ward is far from the most turnover-prone quarterback the Jaguars have played this season; that distinction goes to Daniel Jones. But he is right near the league average in interception rate, and he has made some egregious decisions with the ball over his last two seasons as a starter. This feels like the perfect week for Anthony Campanile to cook some pressure looks up to confuse Ward, and Bates is a natural playmaker. I think we see his impact right away. Parker Washington Catches 2 TDs The Titans' defense has been ... not very good against slot receivers this season. The Titans rank in the bottom-5 in the NFL against slot targets in each of the following categories: yards per play allowed, yards after the catch allowed, yards after the catch over expectation, and average seperation. The Titans have simply been a mess in the slot, even moving long-time outside cornerback Alontae Taylor to the slot despite signing him in March to play on the outside. As a result, I think this is a Parker Washington week. He is the clear No. 1 receiver in the offense, and I think he shakes off some inconsistent moments we have seen as of late and has a huge game against the Titans. Washington is due for a big performance, and I think we see it this Sunday against the Titans. Cam Ward Throws For Fewer Than 150 Yards There have been 275 quarterback performances this season. In just 39 of those performances, we have seen quarterbacks throw for fewer than 150 yards. Cam Ward makes up two of those games, a number that is trumped only by Bo Nix and Malis Willis which is, well, not great company to be in as far as productive gunslingers go. Ward has been more productive and explosive as of late and is coming off one of the best games of his career, but I predict the Jaguars limit Ward to under 150. Ward threw for just 141 yards against the Jaguars in Week 13 a year ago, and the Jaguars limited Daniel Jones and Joe Fagnano to a combined 189 yards over the last eight quarters. The Jaguars' pass defense is clicking, largely due to the work of defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile, and I believe we see it continue this week. Jaguars Limit Tony Pollard to Under 4.0 YPC Titans running back Tony Pollard has been on a tear over the last few weeks. Pollard, who has rushed for 246 yards and five touchdowns over the last two games, broke out of a mid-season skid and has been able to average over 4.0 yards per carry in every single game but two this season. While Pollard has been one of the NFL's more impressive runners over the last few weeks, I expect the Jaguars to be ready to bottle him up on Sunday. Again, I think the Jaguars will play Davis and Godchaux on Sunday. But even if they don't, I do not think the Titans have the offense to keep the Jaguars off-balance enough to run the ball on them. Teams can only run the ball on the Jaguars when the Jaguars are threatened by the early-down pass, and I do not see the Titans having much success there. Walker Little Pitches Another Shutout The Jaguars have seen Walker Little play really, really well over the last few weeks since stepping into the lineup for an injured Anton Harrison. According to NextGenStats, Little has allowed pressure on just 6.4% of his pass blocks, the fifth lowest rate in the league among left tackles (minimum 100 pass blocks). On his 109 pass blocks, his 87.2% 1-on-1 matchup rate is the highest in the league among left tackles; his 6.3% 1-on-1 pressure rate allowed is the third lowest pressure rate allowed in the league. “The experience always helps. Confidence is a heck of a thing, and I think he's the one that said it in an interview that humility helped. Where obviously he became our swing tackle, and all that guy has done is just stay the course," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said on Wednesday. "Like, never got up, too down. He's just very steady. I really like Walker's play demeanor, the look in his eye recently and not taking everything so seriously. He's able to have fun with it. He's out there playing a game that he loves and competes with, but he's playing at a high level right now. He's got confidence, and you can tell.” Little will mostly draw Titans pass-rusher Jacob Martin, who has had a good year. But after strong showings against the Houston Texans' pass-rush duo in London a month ago and then a dominant outing against Trey Hendrickson last week , I think Little has the edge entering Week 10. He is playing some of the best football of his career right now, and I predict it leads to another shutout. Fans wouldn't be blamed for forgetting that we've got football this coming Sunday after days on end filled with rumors and breaking news at the end of every sentence. Not only do the Titans play in Week 10, but they're hosting AFC South-rivals. The Jacksonville Jaguars, one of the most active buyers at the trade deadline, are coming to Nashville to boast their new pickups. The last time Tennessee faced Jacksonville, the Titans lost 41-7 at the very end of the 2025 season. Cam Ward missed the majority of that game after exiting early with a shoulder injury, and his healthy showing tomorrow is the key to a potential Titans upset. Will: Cam Ward stays hot in Carnell Tate's return Ward nearly led Tennessee to a victory over the (now) 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. The Titans falling short 36-43 in overtime was partly due to Ward taking a costly sack late in regulation, but the QB can't at all be blamed for losing a game he kept Tennessee in. With WR1 Carnell Tate trending toward a return, Ward should have all of his weapons in place to put up another promising game. The Titans even kept RB Tony Pollard at the deadline for Ward's own sake. Again, Jacksonville bulked up at the deadline - their defense specifically - but Tennessee leaving the offense untouched said loud and clear that this franchise believes in Ward. With a newly-gutted defense, the Titans will be relying on Ward to try and secure the win. Won't: Jaguars' overhauled defense clicks immediately Directly opposing Ward is that new-look Jags defense. In addition to adding All-Pro S Jessie Bates III, Jacksonville also acquired defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux. That could be one reason among many, but it seems to be the most relevant by far regarding this specific matchup. Prediction: Titans lose, 34-23 At the end of the day on Sunday, I expect Jacksonville will overwhelm Tennessee. I don't believe it will be in blowout fashion, and this is primarily because of the stable flashes of progress Ward showed in Week 8. But between their overhauled defense and Trevor Lawrence manning things under center on offense, the Titans are truly facing a championship contender this week. Perhaps the home field will help blunt the blow, as well as the team debuting their Music City jerseys. I love the jerseys. I like what we saw from Cam Ward in his most recent game. (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jimmy Morris · SB Nation Fri, November 13, 2026 at 4:18 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads If you didn't already know before the last couple of weeks that the Tennessee Titans and Jacksonville Jaguars are in very different places, the two teams' activities around the 2026 NFL trade deadline confirmed it. The Titans traded their two best defensive players for future draft picks. The Jaguars traded future draft picks for three players to solidify their defense. The Titans are 10.5-point home underdogs in this game. As I have said many times this year, that number doesn't feel high enough. This feels like a name-your-number type of game for Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville offense. They are 4th in the league in points per game at 28.6. The Titans defense ranks 22nd, allowing 24.9 points per game. For the Titans offense, the most important thing here is to see Cam Ward build on his performance against the Cincinnati Bengals two weeks ago. You should not expect him to throw for 300 yards again; he has only done that once in his career, but he should be able to be in command of the offense. Brian Daboll pushed the right buttons in that Bengals game. This Jaguars defense is a tougher test, but they are middle of the road against the pass. As much as it pains me to say it, I expect the Jaguars to win this game by at least two touchdowns. Their offense has been really clicking this season, with Lawrence playing the best football of his career. My hope is that the Titans will be able to do enough to make this game hit the over. These newcomers join a team that already holds a three-game lead in its division. They will also line up on the other side of the ball from an offense that is cooking with gas. The fourth-highest-scoring unit in the NFL has flat-out demolished half of its opponents. Trevor Lawrence , somehow, is still somewhat flying under the radar — probably because his offense keeps building such large leads that he does not need to rack up passing numbers in the second halves of these blowouts. Parker Washington has turned into a star, and Bhayshul Tuten emerged as a bona fide No. 1 running back. All of the pieces are in place. Just when it seemed like the Patriots were starting to put everything back together, they hit another rough patch. Just like they did to open the season, they have lost two of their last three games. The only win in that stretch was a five-point squeaker against the lowly Miami Dolphins . The road ahead does not get a whole lot easier with five likely playoff teams on the schedule over the next eight weeks. It is going to be a battle to return to the postseason after last year's run to the Super Bowl. Don't look now, but the Houston Texans are not out of it yet. The AFC South will remain out of reach so long as the Jaguars do not shockingly collapse, so it is Wild Card or bust for a squad that started the year at 0-4. At just 1.5 games back, the Texans are right in the mix. Since that winless first month of the season, the Texans have won three of four and took two of those games in blowout fashion. They just put up a season-high 44 points on the bottom-dwelling Los Angeles Chargers in a game that emphasized how far C.J. Stroud has come as a quarterback. He continues to play the best football of his career and is not even remotely the reason why the Texans are still two games under .500. Tank Dell's return to the wide receiver group and Marvin Harrison Jr.'s addition about a month ago also gave him a deep stable of pass-catchers to target, and he is cashing in. Losses are rare in the NFC North. At least one team has to add one to their tally in Week 10, though. The Packers are the only team with three losses, so every matchup means a little bit more to them as they try to work their way out of the shallow basement of the NFL's best division — one that could send all four teams to the postseason . They will have vengeance on their minds on Sunday as they seek to get payback for what the Minnesota Vikings did to them in a stunning second-half comeback in Week 1. But they will have to do so against a Vikings offense that should be far better the rest of the season now that Kirk Cousins is in at quarterback. Week 10 injury report:

That, of course, with quarterback Malik Willis and standout defensive lineman Zach Sieler in the lineup, with both now on injured reserve. The Colts also have their issues, having traded four veterans — Quenton Nelson, DeForrest Buckner, Keenan Allen and Josh Downs — in the midst of a wildly disappointing season that's already seen GM Chris Ballard lose his job. The Colts did retain star running back Jonathan Taylor and veteran defensive tackle Grove Stewart, who had been rumored to be on the move, and it's not like they're playing for draft position since their 2027 first-round pick belongs to the New York Jets as the result of the Sauce Gardner trade that keeps looking worse every day. Tuesday could significantly affect the odds for this weekend's game, but for now, the Colts are slightly favored.

They got close against the Cowboys, but the seventh loss this season marks doom. The Dolphins are coming to town, so this might be their best shot at win number three on the year. FanDuel Sportsbook favors the Colts to start with a 2.5-point spread advantage. The money line is -138 while the over/under sits at 43.5. The Colts had a rough Sunday. As bad as it was, they still had a legitimate chance to pull out a victory. The offense struggled mightily in the first half but put it all together to take a lead with less than two minutes in regulation. With their first-round pick belonging to the Jets, they would prefer it doesn't reach higher than it needs to. The team is entering "pride" season, as that is all that may be left to play for. away.source: The Palm Beach Post on MSN
away.blurb: Wide receiver Chris Bell has been limited in practice this week with a knee issue. Hafley said he would not practice on Friday and is doubtful, but he has not been ruled out. Hafley said Bell got hit in the leg during practice and it did not have to do with his prior knee injury. Hafley said he expects Chop Robinson and Josh Uche to step up in defensive lineman Zach Sieler's absence . Sieler is out for the season after season-ending biceps surgery. This article originally appeared on Palm Beach Post: Dolphins injury report: QB Malik Willis, C Aaron Brewer out vs. Colts Miami Dolphins All-Pro center Aaron Brewer remains in concussion protocol and will not play against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Coach Jeff Hafley said Andrew Meyer will start in Brewer's place. Meyer, who started a game last season, has worked closely with Kyle McCord since the quarterback's arrival from Green Bay. McCord will be making his first NFL start in place of Malik Willis, who is on injured reserve. "He's done a nice job. Have a lot of confidence in Meyer," Hafley said. Hafley also said his new quarterback has a "very calm confidence" about him. "He's got a quiet leadership about him. He's got a confidence to him. He's very calm in the huddle. And he seems to be grasping everything really well," Hafley said. "I think he's done a really good job in the two practices that we've had. (Friday's) a big day again, getting more in the red zone and polishing up some stuff. "But again, this will be a process, right? I'm not going to expect him to look perfect. There's going to be hopefully some really good moments for him and then there's going to be some that we're going to have to continue to grow in these next games. But I'm excited for him and I appreciate how he's worked, attacked the game plan and how he's kind of communicating and developing chemistry with the players around him in the huddle." "The way Chop's playing and really practicing, I think he's a great example of what it's supposed to look like," Hafley said. "And I think he's going to grow into one of those roles."

away.headline: Breaking Down the Dolphins Saturday Updates for the Indianapolis Game
away.blurb: Reagor being elevated would seem to indicate that wide receiver Chris Bell indeed will be inactive after being listed as doubtful on the final injury report of the week with a knee injury that kept him out of practice Thursday and Friday. Along with potentially getting snaps at wide receiver, Reagor also becomes an option to return punts and/or kickoffs. Bell will be joining Jalen Wayne, who was ruled out Friday, on the inactive list. Reagor will join Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas, Kevin Coleman Jr. and Jalen Tolbert on the game-day roster. Lastly, as expected, the Dolphins didn't activate cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. off PUP and officially was downgraded to out on the injury report. The Miami Dolphins made the expected moves Saturday ahead of their Week 10 game against the Indianapolis Colts, but they still have an opening to be filled at some point. The Dolphins announced early Saturday afternoon they had signed kicker Zane Gonzalez to the 53-man roster off the practice squad, along with elevating quarterback Brady Cook and wide receiver Jalen Reagor. Head coach Jeff Hafley already had indicated earlier this week the team would be signing Gonzalez to the active roster, which was the only way he could kick again for Miami this season after exhausting his three allowed elevations. The move can be questioned based on Gonzalez missed a field goal each of the past two games, although special teams coordinator Chris Tabor said Thursday the miss against the New England in Week 8 was more about the whole operation than a Gonzalez mistake. "I think he's a good player," Tabor said. "I think he's a player that, yes, he missed a kick he should have made. We can all agree about that and Zane would too. In my eyes, that's kind of his first miss. I know on stats that it's two, sometimes there's other things that go on. I'm just not really, I'm not a guy that just pushes players away. He's been on the street for six weeks, seven weeks, and this was his third week back, so I think that he's still working to get to where he needs to be, right? I got a lot of confidence in him and we're working hard at getting better. I look forward to watching him kick this weekend. I got a lot of confidence in him, and it's real easy for me." The signing of Gonzalez put the Dolphins at 52 players on the active roster after the moves this week that saw QB Malik Willis and DT Zach Sieler go on injured reserve, CB Reese Taylor getting waived, and DT Keith Cooper Jr. signed off the Carolina Panthers practice squad. Cook was on the active roster earlier this season before being waived and re-signed to the practice squad, and he seemed like a logical choice to be re-signed to the 53 if he's going to back up new starter Kyle McCord for the next four games while Willis is on IR. Technically, the Dolphins don't have to make that decision until after Cook has been elevated three times, which woud come after the Week 12 game against the New York Jets. away.headline: First Injury Report of Week 10: Dolphins Offense Could Be Even More Short-Handed Against Indianapolis
away.blurb: The Dolphins released their first injury report of Week 10 on Wednesday and what stood out was center Aaron Brewer not practice because of a concussion. While it's too early to rule out Brewer for the game against the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium, the fact he didn't practice Wednesday doesn't bode well. Based on the Return to Play protocol for players dealing with concussions, it's probably a must that Brewer practice Thursday on a limited basis for him to have a chance to play against the Colts. Robinson had to sit out the Week 2 game against San Francisco, while Proctor missed the Week 8 game against the New England Patriots. It should be noted that ahead of that New England game, cornerback JuJu Brents also missed the Wednesday practice because of a concussion before he was limited Thursday and a full participant Friday. He ended up playing against the Patriots. The other issue to monitor on offense involves rookie wide receiver Chris Bell, who is back on the injury report with limited participation in practice because of a knee issue. And rest assured the Dolphins will be very careful not to rush him into action. The Dolphins unfortunately are becoming accustomed to having to deal with concussions, as both edge defender Chop Robinson and guard Kadyn Proctor missed a game this season because of that issue. Brewer played every snap against the Lions during the 19-9 loss Sunday, so this llikely was another case of him reporting symptoms the following day. The other player on the 53-man roster who didn't practice Wednesday was rookie tight end Will Kacmarek, who is dealing with quad/knee issues. If he were unable to play against Indianapolis, it likely would mean more reps for fellow rookie Seydou Traore, who's gotten more involved on offense is recent weeks and also would mean an appearance by waiver wire pick-up Justin Joly. Bell, who is nearing the one-year anniversary of the torn ACL he sustained in his final season at Louisville, last was on the injury report before the Week 5 game against the Cincinnati Bengals. It's logical to think, though not certain, he's dealing with some soreness in his surgically repaired knee. That obviously isn't a great development after he wasn't on the injury report at all for the past three games. Bell played 36 offensive snaps against Detroit after playing 45 against the New England Patriots. He was targeted only once against the Lions, the result being an incomplete pass. Panthers vs. Saints Final Score Prediction SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan broke down this game in his Road to 272 Bets column, in which he picks each game every week: This is a terrible matchup between two NFC South teams, and there's not a convincing argument to bet on either of them in what's a near coin-flip game. With that being said, there is an argument to be made for betting the OVER. As bad as both teams are, the offenses for each of them have played better than their defenses. They enter this game ranking 13th and 22nd in EPA per play but 22nd and 25th in opponent EPA per play. Things get even worse for both defenses when you consider their respective success rates, which rank 24th and 30th in the NFL. There is also one glaring weakness of both defenses, and it's their inability to get off the field on third down. away.headline: Saints Injury Report: Tyler Shough Loses Two Key Protectors Against Panthers
away.blurb: Head coach Kellen Moore ruled out multiple players with injuries, including two starting offensive linemen: center Erik McCoy (bicep) and right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee). The team will also miss rookie running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) and second-round defensive lineman Christen Miller (knee). The Saints got a little more than three quarters of football out of their starting five offensive linemen last week before McCoy exited with an injury. Then Fuaga suffered a knee sprain in practice. Moore said Fuaga isn’t expected to miss enough time to land on injured reserve, but McCoy’s outlook is less certain. A few other players are questionable for Sunday’s game with the Carolina Panthers. Running back Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) is the big name, but cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. is one to watch, too. We’ll find out for sure when the inactives list is published on Sunday. The New Orleans Saints will be short-handed in Sunday’s rivalry game with the Carolina Panthers , with the heaviest hits being on the offensive line. Saints Offensive Line Facing Major Adjustments The Saints got more than three quarters of action from their starting offensive line in last week's win over the Cleveland Browns before McCoy exited with a biceps injury. The situation worsened when Fuaga suffered a knee sprain during practice, leaving New Orleans without two important pieces of its offensive front. Moore indicated Fuaga's injury is not expected to require a stint on injured reserve, although McCoy's recovery timeline remains uncertain. McCoy's absence could prove particularly challenging as he plays a critical role in identifying defensive fronts, communicating protection adjustments and helping maintain continuity across the offensive line as the center. Without him, New Orleans must rely on Cesar Ruiz to handle those responsibilities while adjusting to a reshuffled interior with Jeremiah Wright taking Ruiz’s spot at right guard. Fuaga's injury creates another significant concern at right tackle, where Asim Richards could be called upon to step into the starting lineup. The Saints also dealt with injuries involving left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. (ankle) and guard David Edwards (knee) throughout the week. While both returned to full participation Friday, it’s another sign that this unit is not even close to 100%. Even with Banks and Edwards, losing two starters makes it hard for an offensive line that has struggled with pass protection and consistency in the running game. away.headline: Report: Saints to activate Travis Etienne Jr. for Week 10 vs. Panthers
away.blurb: In his first three games to start 2026 in New Orleans, Etienne rushed for 128 yards and averaged 4.3 per carry. He also had 11 receptions for 51 yards. Etienne was having his best game as a Saint in Week 3 against the Raiders, rushing for 57 yards, before going down with a hamstring injury in the third quarter. He was placed on injured reserve the following week and has missed the last five games before returning to practice this week. By the end of the week, he was practicing in full capacity and was officially listed as questionable to face Carolina on the week's final injury report. As expected, the Ringer's Tom Pelissero reports the New Orleans Saints plan to activate running back Travis Etienne Jr. from injured reserve for their game against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. The 3-5 Saints and Panthers play for sole possession of first place in the NFC South division. This will be the first action for Etienne since Week 3 back on Sept. 27 against the Raiders . Etienne, 27, was signed to a three-year contract by the Saints in free agency last offseason. He was expected to be the lead back for a New Orleans offense that ranked 28th in rushing production in 2025, the team's first year under head coach Kellen Moore. Etienne starred at Jennings High School in Louisiana before playing collegiately for the Clemson Tigers as a three-time All-American and twice ACC Offensive Player of the Year. A first round choice of the Jacksonville Jaguars in the 2021 NFL Draft, Etienne rushed for over 1,000 yards three times in four seasons between 2022 and 2025 before being signed by the Saints in free agency. Etienne is expected to share backfield duties with Audric Estime and Alvin Kamara against the Panthers. Estime is coming off 72 rushing yards last week against the Browns, a season-high for any New Orleans runner. Kamara has 157 rushing yards and an average of 3.3 per carry over seven games this season. The Saints come into Week 10 ranked 26th in rushing with an average of 95.3 yards per game and 3.8 per carry. They'll face a Panthers defense ranked 28th against the run, giving up 4.6 per rush and an average of 133.4 yards per contest. home.headline: Saints Injury Report: Tyler Shough Loses Two Key Protectors Against Panthers
home.blurb: Head coach Kellen Moore ruled out multiple players with injuries, including two starting offensive linemen: center Erik McCoy (bicep) and right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee). The team will also miss rookie running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) and second-round defensive lineman Christen Miller (knee). The Saints got a little more than three quarters of football out of their starting five offensive linemen last week before McCoy exited with an injury. Then Fuaga suffered a knee sprain in practice. Moore said Fuaga isn’t expected to miss enough time to land on injured reserve, but McCoy’s outlook is less certain. A few other players are questionable for Sunday’s game with the Carolina Panthers. Running back Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) is the big name, but cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. is one to watch, too. We’ll find out for sure when the inactives list is published on Sunday. The New Orleans Saints will be short-handed in Sunday’s rivalry game with the Carolina Panthers , with the heaviest hits being on the offensive line. Saints Offensive Line Facing Major Adjustments The Saints got more than three quarters of action from their starting offensive line in last week's win over the Cleveland Browns before McCoy exited with a biceps injury. The situation worsened when Fuaga suffered a knee sprain during practice, leaving New Orleans without two important pieces of its offensive front. Moore indicated Fuaga's injury is not expected to require a stint on injured reserve, although McCoy's recovery timeline remains uncertain. McCoy's absence could prove particularly challenging as he plays a critical role in identifying defensive fronts, communicating protection adjustments and helping maintain continuity across the offensive line as the center. Without him, New Orleans must rely on Cesar Ruiz to handle those responsibilities while adjusting to a reshuffled interior with Jeremiah Wright taking Ruiz’s spot at right guard. Fuaga's injury creates another significant concern at right tackle, where Asim Richards could be called upon to step into the starting lineup. The Saints also dealt with injuries involving left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. (ankle) and guard David Edwards (knee) throughout the week. While both returned to full participation Friday, it’s another sign that this unit is not even close to 100%. Even with Banks and Edwards, losing two starters makes it hard for an offensive line that has struggled with pass protection and consistency in the running game. home.headline: Saints Face Offensive Line Injuries Entering Week 10
home.blurb: Finally, coming out of the bye, the New Orleans Saints ' injury issues were getting better, and the team was set to get some very important returns. WR Jordyn Tyson made his first career start, and LT Kelvin Banks Jr. returned against the Cleveland Browns. Both players made massive impacts on the Saints offense and were an important reason why the Saints were able to win that game. New Orleans is also soon getting RB Travis Etienne back, completing the offense and making it fully healthy for the first time this season. Well, until recently. Just when pieces were on their way back, the Saints have lost their starting right tackle and center. Taliese Fuaga popped onto the injury report this week and has been unable to practice since. Being out of Friday's practice meant he was likely going to miss Sunday's important game against the Carolina Panthers, and that's exactly what ended up happening. Then, for McCoy, he was injured near the end of the Browns game. We knew right away that he would be out for a good amount of time. The Saints also ruled out CJ Donaldson and Christen Miller. The offensive line has had a number of issues throughout this season, including some injuries, but this is the worst it's been. Cesar Ruiz will fill in at center, Jeremiah Wright at guard, and likely Asim Richards at RT. Some movements across the offensive line could actually bring some success if it works out, but it's more likely mistakes will arise that really hurt the Saints' offense. The good news is we will finally get some answers about the future. Ruiz is out of contract soon, and so is McCoy. With the veteran center's injuries, the Saints will need to figure out a plan for his replacement, and Ruiz could be that if he does well. Before the NFL, Ruiz only played center in his career, so that's the position he us is more of a natural at. Then, at RG, we get to see more Wright snaps, which could result in him proving he should be the starter next season. home.headline: Report: Saints to activate Travis Etienne Jr. for Week 10 vs. Panthers
home.blurb: In his first three games to start 2026 in New Orleans, Etienne rushed for 128 yards and averaged 4.3 per carry. He also had 11 receptions for 51 yards. Etienne was having his best game as a Saint in Week 3 against the Raiders, rushing for 57 yards, before going down with a hamstring injury in the third quarter. He was placed on injured reserve the following week and has missed the last five games before returning to practice this week. By the end of the week, he was practicing in full capacity and was officially listed as questionable to face Carolina on the week's final injury report. As expected, the Ringer's Tom Pelissero reports the New Orleans Saints plan to activate running back Travis Etienne Jr. from injured reserve for their game against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday. The 3-5 Saints and Panthers play for sole possession of first place in the NFC South division. This will be the first action for Etienne since Week 3 back on Sept. 27 against the Raiders . Etienne, 27, was signed to a three-year contract by the Saints in free agency last offseason. He was expected to be the lead back for a New Orleans offense that ranked 28th in rushing production in 2025, the team's first year under head coach Kellen Moore. Etienne starred at Jennings High School in Louisiana before playing collegiately for the Clemson Tigers as a three-time All-American and twice ACC Offensive Player of the Year. A first round choice of the Jacksonville Jaguars in the 2021 NFL Draft, Etienne rushed for over 1,000 yards three times in four seasons between 2022 and 2025 before being signed by the Saints in free agency. Etienne is expected to share backfield duties with Audric Estime and Alvin Kamara against the Panthers. Estime is coming off 72 rushing yards last week against the Browns, a season-high for any New Orleans runner. Kamara has 157 rushing yards and an average of 3.3 per carry over seven games this season. The Saints come into Week 10 ranked 26th in rushing with an average of 95.3 yards per game and 3.8 per carry. They'll face a Panthers defense ranked 28th against the run, giving up 4.6 per rush and an average of 133.4 yards per contest. picks.blurb: Pick Six: Buffalo Bills at New York Jets - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football College football live updates FAA ground stop updates SEC moves Ole Miss-OU to Sunday Colorado ends Houston's CFP hopes Pick Six: Buffalo Bills at New York Jets ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - JANUARY 04: Running back Ray Davis #22 of the Buffalo Bills runs the ball during the fourth quarter against the New York Jets at Highmark Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. The Bills defeated the Jets 35-8. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bent Double · SB Nation Fri, November 13, 2026 at 4:00 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Jets will be a home underdog against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, having lost seven of their last eight games. Other than a last-gasp loss to the Patriots in week four, the Bills' record is unblemished this year. Surely the Jets can't pull off an upset, can they? Here are six storylines to watch as New York seeks to flip their season on its head: It's a trap! America is already looking ahead to the Bills-Chiefs game scheduled to take place in the evening of Thanksgiving Thursday. While Buffalo has two games to play between now and then, they will feel good about their chances of still only having one loss after playing the Jets this week and Miami next week. Kansas City has lost just twice so this could be decisive in the race for the AFC's top seed. We've seen situations like this before though. While the Jets are rarely the team to take advantage of the opportunity, their profile as a team that has kept a lot of games close and come up just short in the end could make them dangerous if the Bills get complacent. And if they did get complacent, who could blame them? After all, the last time these teams met, the Bills rested all of their starters and still won 35-8. Then again, that was a very different Jets team too. The only current non-offensive line starters who started that game are Harrison Phillips, Jamien Sherwood and Adonai Mitchell. Can Mitchell bounce back? It's become traditional this year to have at least one high profile player that doesn't get the ball on offense. Last week, it was Adonai Mitchell, a player who seven days earlier, had posted the best numbers of his career. The Jets really seem to be struggling with the whole "many mouths to feed" aspect of having provided their quarterback with an adequate number of pass catching weapons for the first time in several seasons. However, Mitchell not seeing the ball last week was not for the want of trying as he was thrown to seven times. Opening drive success We could easily spend column inches here talking about why the Jets can't convert in the red zone, or how they shouldn't abandon the running game, or when are they ever going to intercept another pass, but how about we discuss something they have actually been doing well? For each of the past five games, the Jets have driven downfield and scored on their opening possession, which has played a big part in them still being competitive heading into the second half of each game. So, now we have to ask the question – can this continue? And…how will the team react if it doesn't? This isn't the first time in recent memory that the offensive has looked good early on in games, and executed the scripted part of the gameplan effectively, only to then go on to struggle in the second half when points are needed to convert wins. Back in 2020, where Adam Gase's Jets were in danger of going winless until very late in the season, they actually scored eight times in a row on their opening drive. The current decision makers would ideally not like to have too many similarities to that 2020 team. Gregory Rousseau's ascent to super-stardom The biggest threat on the Bills defense is obviously edge rusher Gregory Rousseau, who is having a monster year. After just eight games, Rousseau has already tied his career-high with eight sacks, while also doubling his career mark for passes defensed with another eight. Rousseau primarily lines up on the left, so it will be mostly up to Armand Membou to try and keep him quiet. Rousseau had a two sack game against the Jets in his second season in 2022, but surprisingly otherwise only has one sack in eight other games against the Jets. The Bills are 7-2 in these matchups, though. Having not been traded, is Will McDonald's role going to change? The Jets opted not to trade former first round pick Will McDonald during the week, despite reports of interest from a number of teams. Head coach Aaron Glenn has been suggesting McDonald is still very much in the Jets plans for the rest of this season, and he is of course under contract for next year after New York exercised his fifth year option. He even implied McDonald had earned a bigger role. McDonald's defensive snap count percentage has dropped from 66% in both 2024 and 2025 to just 46% in 2026 and, even more confoundingly, his percentage of run snaps has increased. Will an increase in playing time for McDonald happen on Sunday? And, if it does, are we destined to see diminishing returns in regard to his production? What's the plan for the secondary? A matchup against the team with the number one offense in the entire NFL is not really the ideal time to experiment with line-up changes but the Jets are desperately striving for more consistency from their back seven, in addition to having an undermanned front that is struggling to stop the run. Having missed a meeting and made some on-field mistakes, the previous starting slot corner – Jarvis Brownlee Jr. – is in the doghouse. However, rookie D'Angelo Ponds has looked overmatched at times which is hardly surprising given how he is learning a new position and missed half of training camp. New York also experimented with using Minkah Fitzpatrick in the slot on Sunday, elevating Malachi Moore into the lineup at safety for basically the first time all year. Could this be the answer? Time will tell. Let us know how you see things going in Sunday's game in the comments section…

away.headline: Bills starting tackle misses practice as four offensive linemen deal with injuries
away.blurb: Starting right tackle Spencer Brown was the only Bills player who did not practice Thursday because of an ankle injury. Brown was listed as a limited participant during Wednesday's walkthrough, when practice participation was estimated. The Bills have four starting offensive linemen on their injury report, including left tackle Dion Dawkins (rib), left guard Alec Anderson (ankle) and center Connor McGovern (neck). All three were limited Wednesday and Thursday. Buffalo also listed cornerback Christian Benford as a limited participant for the second consecutive day because of a wrist injury . Benford injured his right wrist against Minnesota, underwent an X-ray at halftime and returned before leaving again in the third quarter. Tight end Dalton Kincaid (ankle) was limited Wednesday and Thursday, while defensive tackle Greg Gaines (calf) was a full participant both days after missing two consecutive games. Defensive back Sam Franklin Jr . was added to Thursday's injury report with a shoulder injury and was limited. Wide receiver Garrett Wilson was limited for the second consecutive day because of a concussion that forced him to miss Sunday's loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. Defensive tackle Harrison Phillips (ankle) and linebacker Trevin Wallace (groin) did not practice for the second consecutive day. Now four starters are dealing with injuries heading into Sunday's game against the New York Jets. Brown returned against Minnesota after missing Buffalo's previous game against Baltimore because of a back injury. The Bills (7-1) visit the Jets (2-7) at 1 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 15, at MetLife Stadium. The Jets have multiple several injury concerns. Cornerback Jarvis Brownlee Jr. was also absent Thursday because of an illness. Both teams will release their final injury reports Friday, including game status designations for Sunday's game.

away.headline: Vikings-Bills Final Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, Kyler Murray is out as expected, as are both Demond Claiborne and Jauan Jennings. Claiborne suffered a knee injury in practice and from Kevin O’Connell’s comments on Saturday, could be out for a while. It wouldn’t be surprising therefore if he was placed on Injured Reserve. It doesn’t appear at the moment that Jennings’ calf injury is a longer-term concern, but we may learn more about that next week. Beyond that, safeties Theo Jackson and Jay Ward are questionable for Monday night. I’m guessing at least one of them will play, but KOC also talked about potentially having Jacob Thomas and/or Tavierre Thomas on the active roster for Monday night to fill in at safety and special teams. For the Bills, backup wide receiver Joshua Palmer is out. But they also have two starting offensive linemen listed as questionable- left tackle Dion Dawkins and left guard Alec Anderson. Dawkins has not practiced all week with a rib injury, so he would seem to be less likely than normal to start with that designation. Anderson was upgraded to limited on Saturday after missing Thursday and Friday practices with an ankle injury. My guess is that if either of them play on Monday night they will be less than 100%, so the left side of the Bills’ offensive line could be a bit more vulnerable than normal. Beyond that, Tyrell Shavers and Jordan Hancock are listed as questionable, but the Bills will need to activate them from the PUP list and IR for them to be eligible to play on Monday night. We’ll see if that happens. Alec Anderson, Spencer Brown, Dion Dawkins, and Connor McGovern were all limited Wednesday. Anderson and Brown were listed with ankle injuries, Dawkins with a rib injury, and McGovern with a neck injury. Christian Benford was also limited by a wrist injury. The cornerback dealt with the issue during Monday's game against Minnesota. It caused him to briefly leave the game, and his availability will be worth watching as the week progresses. Tight end Dalton Kincaid rounded out the limited participants, appearing on the report with an ankle injury. Kincaid also briefly left Monday's game after appearing to roll his ankle but returned to finish the contest. It's also important to note that the chest injury he had been listed for in weeks past seems to no longer be an issue. Despite concerns about the limited players, there was some positive news on the defensive side of the ball. Defensive tackle Greg Gaines was a full participant despite dealing with a calf injury that kept him out of the previous two games. Defensive lineman T.J. picks.blurb: Seahawks vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 10 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football College football live updates FAA ground stop updates SEC moves Ole Miss-OU to Sunday Colorado ends Houston's CFP hopes Seahawks vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 10 Chris Spiering, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Wed, November 11, 2026 at 10:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Seattle Seahawks have a golden opportunity to make a statement against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10. Seattle is coming off a quieter offensive performance against the Arizona Cardinals, but this matchup presents a chance for the Seahawks to get back on track in a big way. The Raiders have one of the worst defenses in the NFL, particularly when it comes to stopping the run. Meanwhile, rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza is preparing for his first NFL start against a Seattle defense that has been one of the toughest units in the league. I expect the Seahawks to take advantage of both matchups. Here are four bold predictions for Sunday's game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Bold Prediction No. 4: Jadarian Price scores his first NFL touchdown Credit: Matt Kartozian-Imagn Images This could finally be the game when Jadarian Price gets into the end zone for the first time in his NFL career. It's been a challenging rookie season for the first-round pick, who has yet to find his footing in Seattle's backfield. However, this matchup could be exactly what he needs to change the trajectory of his season. The Raiders have struggled mightily against opposing running backs, and Price should have opportunities to make an impact. With Zach Charbonnet also back in the backfield, Seattle has more options to attack Las Vegas. It is expected Price will take advantage of his opportunities and finally get that first NFL touchdown. Bold Prediction No. 3: Jaxon Smith-Njigba records 10+ catches, 125+ yards, and at least one TD Even though Seattle should have plenty of success running the football, that doesn't mean Jaxon Smith-Njigba won't have a monster afternoon. JSN is coming off a relatively quiet performance against the Cardinals, finishing with seven catches for 51 yards without a touchdown. That is not the kind of production we've grown accustomed to seeing from one of the NFL's best wide receivers. I expect a much different performance against Las Vegas. The Raiders have struggled to contain opposing offenses. I think he gets back to dominating opposing secondaries. Bold Prediction No. 2: Seahawks' rushing attack finally has a monster game The Raiders are allowing a league-leading 151.2 rushing yards per game. That's an invitation for Seattle to establish its ground game and take advantage of one of the NFL's worst run defenses. Seattle averages 110 yards on the ground. The Seahawks have yet to consistently get their rushing attack going, but this is the perfect opportunity to change that. With rookie Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet back from injury, Seattle has the personnel to make life miserable for Las Vegas. It shouldn't matter who is getting the carries. I expect the Seahawks to pound the rock throughout the afternoon and finish with close to 200 rushing yards. And remember, I still expect Smith-Njigba to have a monster game through the air. Seattle could realistically finish with more than 450 total yards of offense if everything goes according to plan. Bold Prediction No. 1: Fernando Mendoza has a nightmare game in his first NFL start Welcome to the NFL, Fernando Mendoza . The rookie quarterback is getting his first opportunity to lead the Raiders after the organization made a major change at the position. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings . Unfortunately, his first start comes against a Seahawks defense that can make life extremely difficult for opposing quarterbacks. Mendoza does have some talented tight ends to work with, but Las Vegas' receiving corps is underwhelming. Seattle should be able to make things uncomfortable for the rookie, particularly if its pass rush can consistently generate pressure. It wouldn't be surprising if Mendoza throws a touchdown pass at some point. However, I expect the Raiders' offense to struggle for most of the afternoon. The prediction is that Mendoza finishes with fewer than 175 passing yards and completes less than 65% of his attempts. His first NFL start will be a difficult learning experience, and Seattle's defense will be the biggest reason why. away.headline: Seahawks’ Mike Macdonald Gives Strong Jalen Milroe Statement Amid QB Injuries
away.blurb: As for Milroe, the first-team repetitions are a chance to show he can handle more than a limited package constructed around his athleticism. Seattle will start Lock against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 15, with Darnold ruled out because of quadriceps and rib injuries. The veteran has been limited in practice while managing an elbow injury and the oblique issue he suffered against the Arizona Cardinals. Klint Kubiak Speaks out on Facing Seahawks in Week 10 Seahawks' Mike Macdonald Gives Strong Jalen Milroe Statement Amid QB Injuries Unlock the latest Heavy on Seahawks news — direct to your inbox. The Seattle Seahawks have spent the past two weeks dealing with injuries to their top two quarterbacks. That's given Jalen Milroe more time with the starting offense. And head coach Mike Macdonald likes what he has seen. Speaking with reporters Friday, Nov. 13, Macdonald delivered strong praise for the second-year quarterback's work while Drew Lock and Sam Darnold recover from injuries. "I think it's appropriate to say Jalen has done a tremendous job when he's been in there with the ones," Macdonald said. The coach went on to laud Milroe's work ethic, accuracy and decision-making. He specifically highlighted the young quarterback's ability to deliver throws on time. It's a welcome assessment for a player who has waited for a chance to show his ability for much of his NFL career. Seahawks' Jalen Milroe Impresses Mike Macdonald With First-Team Offense Milroe has taken snaps with Seattle's starters during the past two weeks as Lock works through elbow and oblique injuries. Macdonald made it obvious Friday that the extra work hasn't been wasted. The coach described Milroe as decisive with the football and praised his execution when called upon to replace Lock during practice. The comments came in a Nov. 13 report from Seahawks.com's John Boyle . Seattle selected Milroe in the third round of the 2025 NFL draft, taking the former Alabama quarterback with the No. 92 overall pick. His rookie season showed very little game experience. Milroe appeared in three regular-season contests, carrying the ball three times for four yards without attempting a pass. Heading into 2026, he sat behind Darnold and Lock on the depth chart The latest injuries have changed his practice workload, though they haven't produced an official quarterback change. Seahawks Have More QB Questions Before Raiders Game Lock is also feeling his own physical problems. Still, Macdonald put forth confidence Friday that Lock can handle another start, so Milroe is an important insurance option. If Lock cannot finish Sunday's game, Seattle could be forced to turn to the former Alabama standout against Las Vegas. Milroe has now prepared for that possibility for weeks. Darnold's recovery is undetermined, although Seattle has a Week 11 bye that gives its injured quarterbacks extra time to heal. Milroe's future still depends on the health of the players ahead of him. away.headline: Week 10 Injury Report: Seahawks at Raiders
away.blurb: The Seahawks will be getting a couple of players back from injury for Sunday's game in Las Vegas, with outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu and receiver Rashid Shaheed both ready to return after missing the past two games with ankle and knee injuries, respectively. The Seahawks will still be without four players who also missed last week's game: left tackle Charles Cross (ankle), quarterback Sam Darnold (ribs/quadriceps), guard Quenton Nelson (knee) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger), all of whom were ruled out on Friday's injury report. Cross, who was able to practice Thursday on a limited basis, should be able to make it back after Seattle's Week 11 bye, Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said. Quarterback Drew Lock was limited all week due to elbow and oblique injuries, as was expected coming into the week, but he has no injury designation, and the plan is still for him to make his second straight start in place of Darnold. Defensive tackle Jarran Reed , who did not practice Wednesday or Thursday due to a personal matter, was back at practice Friday and will play, Macdonald said, clarifying that it was a good personal matter. For the Raiders, defensive tackle Thomas Booker (ankle) and receiver Dont'e Thornton (back), are listed as questionable. Thursday's report featured only a couple of changes for the Seahawks, including a significant one for the offensive line, with left tackle Charles Cross , who has missed the past two games with an ankle injury, listed as limited after not practicing Wednesday. The only other changes were that tight end AJ Barner , who was a full participant Wednesday with a finger injury, has been removed from the injury report altogether, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who got a rest day on Wednesday, was a full participant. As expected, quarterback Drew Lock was limited again, as has been the plan as he prepares to start while dealing with elbow and oblique injuries. Receiver Rashid Shaheed , who is trying to make his way back from a knee injury that kept him out of two games, was a full participant for the second day in a row, while Uchenna Nwosu , who is trying to get back from an ankle injury, was limited for the second day in a row. Defensive tackle Leonard Williams , who is dealing with a stinger, was a non-participant for the second day in a row, as were quarterback Sam Darnold and left guard Quenton Nelson , both of whom have already been ruled out of Week 10 by Mike Macdonald. For the Raiders, defensive tackle Folorunso Fatukasi (shoulder, back) was upgraded from limited to full participation, while defensive tackle Thomas Booker (ankle) and offensive lineman Trey Zuhn (concussion) were limited for the second straight day. away.blurb: Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Jarran Reed both sat for non-injury reasons. That's the easy stuff. The pool of limited players includes Anthony Bradford (knee), Derick Hall (back) , Drew Lock (right elbow, oblique), Uchenna Nwosu (ankle), and Connor O'Toole (foot). Offhand, I would expect all five of those players to play on Sunday, but any injury is noteworthy. Nwosu's return to practice is particularly significant, as he attempted a similar timeline last week with a limited practice on Wednesday before getting banished back to DNP the next two days. Hopefully this time, whatever setback or occurrence caused him to hit the bench doesn't happen and he's able to progress. The other injuries strike me as management ones. Thomas Booker (ankle) and Folorunso Fatukasi (shoulder, back) are limited today, and that's not an insignificant one-two, since they combine to be a significant chunk of the Raiders' interior defensive line. Trey Zuhn (concussion) was also limited, the backup center who has gotten little action so far this year. Otherwise, the Raiders look quite healthy and ready to roll. home.blurb: Seahawks-Raiders Wednesday injury report: Leonard Williams still out, Rashid Shaheed returns - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Seattle released the first of the three weekly injury reports, which is headlined by the health of backup quarterback Drew Lock, who is battling a lingering elbow injury and a new oblique injury. Lock was limited in practice on Wednesday, with head coach Mike Macdonald indicating that the veteran is "making good progress" and may start against the Raiders. Whoever is under center will once again be working with a patchwork offensive line as stars Quenton Nelson and Charles Cross did not practice. Nelson is battling a knee injury that might hold him out for his second straight game while Cross has been out with an ankle injury since Week 7. Backup guard Anthony Bradford continues to be hampered by a knee injury and was limited on Wednesday. On the defensive side, Leonard Williams remains out with a stinger that he suffered against the Kansas City Chiefs, and edge rusher Derick Hall was limited with a new back injury. Both would be a massive loss for the Seahawks front that will hope to ruin Raiders' rookie Fernando Mendoza's debut. It wasn't all negative for the Seahawks' defense, though, as signs are trending positive for edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu, who was limited with the ankle injury that's held him out of the team's last two games. The Arizona Cardinals must march the rookie quarterback out to face the Los Angeles Rams (-9.5) and their gruesome twosome of Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett in Week 10. My Rams vs. Cardinals predictions sort out the shifting sands in the NFC West, highlighting some of my best NFL picks for Nov. 15. TOP Pick Rams vs Cardinals prediction: Under 39.5 This total has dropped a touchdown since opening last Sunday night. And it's not just the Arizona Cardinals' QB quandary dragging the number down. Both teams will be without their WR1s, as Los Angeles Rams wideout Puka Nacua and Arizona standout Michael Wilson suffered injuries in Week 9. The cupboard is very bare for Carson Beck , with no Wilson or Kendrick Bourne to throw to, nor does he have RBs Jeremiyah Love and James Conner to help shoulder the offensive load. As for the Rams, their snake-bitten lineup is looking ahead to a much-needed bye in Week 11 . With a spread this size, I expect Los Angeles to try and get up quick and then slow things down in the second half to avoid further casualties. Los Angeles has seen a significant shift in play calling the past three games, upping its run rate from 36% in the first six outings to 48.5% during this current three-game win streak. That's slimmed the Rams' yards per play from 5.9 to 5.2 but upped their average time of possession. Rams vs Cardinals combo A lack of weapons, a rookie QB, and a Rams team trying to get to the bye week without suffering any more hurt. These are all reasons Arizona and Los Angeles stay below the total in Week 10. Blake Corum has scored a touchdown in four straight games, including a receiving TD vs. Arizona in Week 6. He'll get a lot of love in the second half, given the big spread and game script. Tyler Allgeier is now the Cardinals RB1 and is getting a ton of work, with injuries up and down this offense. He's drawn at least three targets in the past three games, and with a rookie QB under center, Allgeier will be a favorite option on short, safe throws. Blake Corum touchdown Tyler Allgeier 10+ receiving yards Rams vs Cardinals touchdown scorer: Blake Corum Blake Corum has enjoyed the Rams' three-game winning streak. He's seen a spike in carries and has struck for a touchdown in each of those outings. Corum does the bulk of his damage in the second half, providing relief for RB1 Kyren Williams , with four of his five total TDs this season coming in the closing 30 minutes. His lone first-half strike was a 15-yard touchdown reception in the Week 6 upset loss to Arizona. Given the beefy spread and the game-script attached to it, Corum will continue to see touches in the final two frames on Sunday. His touchdown forecasts range from 31% to 50% in Week 10.
