picks.blurb: A Duel in the Desert: Los Angeles Rams vs Arizona Cardinals Preview - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football College football live updates FAA ground stop updates SEC moves Ole Miss-OU to Sunday Colorado ends Houston's CFP hopes A Duel in the Desert: Los Angeles Rams vs Arizona Cardinals Preview Nov 8, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay sets the play against the Washington Commanders during the fourth quarter at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Chris Pownall Toussaint Fancher · Last Word on Sports Fri, November 13, 2026 at 11:56 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Los Angeles Rams have an opportunity to avenge their Week 6 loss to the Arizona Cardinals. A Duel in the Desert: Los Angeles Rams vs. Arizona Cardinals Preview Los Angeles has dealt with injuries to several star players throughout the season, but last week brought their worst injury yet. Puka Nacua sustained a blow to his knee on the Rams' final offensive play, which left him with sprains to his posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) ,medial collateral ligament (MCL), and a case of turf toe. Now, Los Angeles must survive until Nacua returns. Head coach Sean McVay knows the Rams have what it takes to beat the Cardinals in their second matchup. "One of the calling cards for our group, and is always an expectation, is we play with passion and energy, and I think we would all agree that (the first game against the Cardinals) wasn't quite up to our standards," McVay said . Los Angeles will likely rely on running 13 personnel while several of their best receivers are sidelined with injuries. Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford must spread the targets in order to keep Arizona's defense off guard. "It's not difficult to pull the trigger, I trust those guys," Stafford said . Nov 8, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford (9) throws the ball against the Washington Commanders during the third quarter at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images While several receivers are injured, the Rams could also become a more defensively minded team. Los Angeles defensive coordinator Chris Shula has done a great job this year. He knows the defense will need to perform even better than it did when the Rams first played the Cardinals. "We didn't get the win so obviously it wasn't good enough," Shula said . Last time these two teams faced each other, the Rams' defensive unit held the Cardinals to six field goals. Last week, Los Angeles welcomed back Myles Garrett after his time on the injured reserve. He finished the game with three sacks, including a strip sack showing his dominance in a Los Angeles jersey for the first time. Garrett's Week 1 performance left much to be desired, especially since he was playing hurt. His return helped Los Angeles defeat the Washington Commanders 20-13. The team is also hoping to get top cornerback Trent McDuffie back from injury. Los Angeles desperately need McDuffie back if they want to keep their season alive. He has missed the past two games after injuring his back in Week 8. This season, McDuffie has been ranked as the third-best cornerback with an 89.8 rating according to Pro Football Focus (PFF). His pass coverage has been exceptional, and he has lived up to expectations in the first year of his massive $124 million deal . Los Angeles is also without their other top cornerback Jaylen Watson , who is out for the season after undergoing shoulder surgery a few weeks ago. Other cornerbacks Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes Jr. have stepped up in his absence, but McDuffie's services are still needed. The Last Word Los Angeles' season could already be over with the number of injuries to key players, but regardless of who's available to play, the Rams must keep pushing for the playoffs. The team is currently riding a three-game winning streak since their loss to the Cardinals. Now, they will have another chance to defeat the Cardinals and former Rams offensive coordinator , Mike LaFleur. The key to this weekend is play-calling. If McVay can keep the Cardinals' defense off balance and use everyone in the pass game, the Rams will be in a strong position to win. Like McVay, Stafford must also be at his best. Coming off an MVP season, Stafford is the glue that must hold the offense together while his best targets are sidelined with injuries. away.headline: Rams Injury Report: Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie Questionable vs. Cardinals
away.blurb: Rams Injury Report: Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie Questionable vs. Cardinals - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Rams Injury Report: Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie Questionable vs. Cardinals The Los Angeles Rams will be managing several injuries on Sunday as they take on the Arizona Cardinals for the second time this season in Week 10. While wide receiver Puka Nacua went on injured reserve this week , left guard Steve Avila has been ruled out as well. Additionally, after making his return in Week 9 against the Washington Commanders, Myles Garrett has officially been listed as questionable but is expected to play, according to head coach Sean McVay. In addition to Garrett, tight end Davis Allen, long snapper Joe Cardona, cornerback Trent McDuffie, and safety Kam Curl were all listed as questionable. After being a non-participant in practice on Thursday, Allen was limited in Friday's practice. With Colby Parkinson not having an injury designation, the Rams should be in a good spot at tight end if Allen is able to go. More importantly, the Rams will be looking to get McDuffie back in action. He was a non-participant in practice on Thursday but was upgraded to limited on Friday. After returning against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 8, McDuffie missed last week's game against the Commanders and has been nursing a back injury. "A lot of it is going to be contingent upon how that limited work goes today. He was rolling, doing a lot of good stuff yesterday," McVay said. "He's chomping at the bit to play, but a lot of that answer will be predicated on how he handles the physical workload today. I think if you asked him, he would say that he's hopeful to be able to play and so are we, but that could change based on how the workout goes." Without Nacua on Sunday, the Rams will be relying heavily on their wide receiver depth . The Rams signed Xavier Smith back to the roster this week and also added Brennan Presley to the active roster. With Avila out as well, Beaux Limmer will likely take his spot at left guard. While the Rams are hoping to get McDuffie back, if he is out, the Rams will rely on Emmanuel Forbes and Josh Wallace for a second straight week. On the Cardinals' side of things, defensive lineman Zach Carter, center Hjalte Froholdt, and interior offensive lineman Jon Gaines have all been ruled out. Additionally, tight end Hunter Long, cornerback Max Melton, offensive lineman Jayden Williams, safety Andrew Wingard, defensive lineman Roy Lopez, and defensive lineman Darius Robinson are all questionable. home.headline: Cardinals QB situation takes stunning turn with Gardner Minshew update: Report
home.blurb: Following their 17-3 road loss Sunday to the Seattle Seahawks, the Arizona Cardinals received a major update on quarterback Gardner Minshew, who may have suffered a season-ending injury. On Monday evening, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that Minshew “is feared to have suffered a torn UCL in his throwing arm.” Rapoport said Minshew suffered the injury before halftime but continued playing through it. According to Rapoport, Minshew will get additional testing done, but the injury could end his season and require a lengthy rehabilitation process. Minshew suffered the injury when he was hit by Seahawks pass rusher Dante Fowler while attempting a pass on the final play of the first half. The Cardinals quarterback grabbed his right arm after the rough hit, but continued to play. In Sunday’s game, Minshew completed 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards and was sacked three times by the Seahawks defense. Seattle held Arizona to just 198 total yards of offense for the game. More news: Chiefs HC Andy Reid Reveals Patrick Mahomes Injury Update Ahead of Falcons Game The devastating update arrived days after the team traded veteran starter Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens. Arizona’s unfortunate situation with Minshew has led to several developments, including Adam Schefter reporting that the team signed Josh Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals’ practice squad. This is Johnson’s 15th team in 14 seasons. According to ESPN , in an initial report on the Cardinals’ injury updates, rookie Carson Beck was expected to start on Sunday. The Cardinals drafted the former Miami Hurricanes quarterback at No. 65 in the 3rd round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Beck led his team to the College Football Playoff National Championship game, which they lost to Fernando Mendoza and the Indiana Hoosiers. The decision to draft Beck was met with mixed reviews, with many sports outlets giving the team a low grade for the pick. NFL.com’s Chad Reuter graded Arizona’s Day 2 picks, including Beck, an “A,” indicating he had “a lot of big-game experience.” However, Reuter also noted that Beck’s decision-making was too inconsistent to be a “surefire starter.” Beck appeared in the NFL Hall of Fame Game this preseason against the Carolina Panthers, throwing for 188 yards and a touchdown in Arizona’s 33-30 loss. With ESPN reporting that Beck is expected to start Sunday, he’s poised to take over for a 3-6 Arizona team, unless they opt to use Johnson instead. Unfortunately, both quarterbacks could face a challenging matchup for the team’s next NFL game. The Cardinals host a Los Angeles Rams team on Sunday, Nov. 15, that has now won three straight games to improve to 5-4 for the season. The Rams also just got back the NFL Defensive Player of the Year, Myles Garrett, who recorded three sacks on Sunday in their 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders, so Beck or Johnson could face a difficult test for his first NFL start. home.headline: Midseason Report Card: Grading Cardinals Coaches Through First Half of 2026
home.blurb: New coordinator Michael Ghobrial has the Cardinals in the top third in the league in kickoff return yardage allowed (25.4). On his own return unit, they're tied for the most amount of kickoff returns for 20+ yards at 39. Punting, meanwhile, is dead last at 43.9 yards per punt. For a team that is tied for the third-most amount of punts, we've got plenty of sample size. As for their punt returns, their 7.9 yards per return is eighth-worst in the NFL. Offensively, the Cardinals have been less than desirable — to say the least. Subpar quarterback play and injuries practically everywhere have really weighed the unit down, though some of LaFleur's play-calling and situational decision-making has also been questionable. How Kirk Cousins Will Impact the Vikings’ Offense in Return to Minnesota Midseason Report Card: Grading Cardinals Coaches Through First Half of 2026 Skip to main content SI.COM ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are halfway through the 2026 season, and quite frankly, have surpassed expectations already. With a 3-6 record, that doesn't exactly roll off the tongue right — though the Cardinals have already reached their projected win total. Signs of a promising future haven't exactly been bountiful, though they've been spotted nonetheless. Before the second half of the regular season gets underway, let's grade the Cardinals' three top coaches: Defensive Coordinator Nick Rallis: C- Arizona Cardinals defensive coordinator Nick Rallis walks the field during training camp at State Farm Stadium in Glendale on Aug 2, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect This was perhaps the toughest evaluation. This was perhaps the toughest evaluation. On one hand, the Cardinals' defense has picked up their play in recent weeks. Rallis has recently found his old (and arguably more successful) calling card in aggressive play-calling and creative sim-pressures. That's led to a fairly drastic step up in production as of late, a positive sign for a coordinator who was very much on the hot seat early this season. However, when taking a step back and evaluating the entire year's performance thus far, it's incredibly hard to forget just how bad Arizona's defense was. Despite the drastic increase in play, the Cardinals have still allowed 30+ points in all but three games this season. Numbers aren't everything, though Arizona still ranks near the bottom of the league in several different categories — both standard and advanced analytics. Right now, it's tough to say Rallis is in jeopardy of losing his job. However, that could easily change with a bad performance or two. Not quite passing, not quite failing. Rallis' recent performances still give hope for a turnaround, but this feels like a very favorable grade. home.blurb: Cardinals – Rams Week 10 injury reports - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL SEC moves Ole Miss-OU to Sunday Colorado ends Houston's CFP hopes Cardinals – Rams Week 10 injury reports ARLINGTON, TX - NOVEMBER 01: Hjalte Froholdt #72 of the Arizona Cardinals speaks to his teammates before kickoff against the Dallas Cowboys during an NFL football game at AT&T Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Barry Shuck · SB Nation Fri, November 13, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Arizona Cardinals are at the halfway point of the season. They need a win very badly. Where does the team head from here? They are facing the Los Angeles Rams once again. In the first match, Arizona's offense dominated the LA defense, but could not score touchdowns and instead came away with six Chad Ryland field goals. away.headline: Cowboys injury report: George Pickens headlines good news before 49ers clash
away.blurb: Starting with that is George Pickens, who missed the Week 9 win over the Colts due to a hamstring issue. But after logging back-to-back limited sessions, it would appear he was on his way back to a return, which turned out to be right, as he practiced in full on Friday and is now off the injury report. That's a major return to the starting lineup obviously, but the storylines don't end there, so let's dive into the final injury report after the week of practice. Let's start with a man who has been a frequent addition on these lists: linebacker DeMarvion Overshown. Overshown missed Week 9 due to a flare-up in his back and a hamstring issue, but practiced in full on both Thursday and Friday after getting in a limited session on Wednesday. He's now off the injury report and is good to go, which is great news against a 49ers team with one of the best running backs in the NFL in Christian McCaffrey, and one of the best tight ends in George Kittle. So while he is healthy, he will have his work cut out for him. This entire defense will, for that matter. The Cowboys are dealing with enough injuries in the secondary, as Jalen Thompson is set to miss his seventh straight game and PJ Locke is out, too. Also, safety Juanyeh Thomas is doubtful after going from a limited session on Thursday to a Friday DNP. But none of this is the biggest deal on the back end. That honor goes to DaRon Bland, who was a surprise addition to Friday's injury report due to an ankle injury. He practiced in full on Wednesday and Thursday, yet was downgraded to limited on Friday, so it feels like his status is in real doubt, although we don't know much about what actually happened. Porter Jr. did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday, but was upgraded to a limited partipant on Friday, so he's progressing in the right direction, although he still has a ways to go before we know he's a true full go. The Dallas Cowboys are right back in striking distance for the NFC East title , as one win will give them the same amount of wins as the New York Giants through 10 weeks. So clearly, a victory on Sunday is crucial, but it won't come easy, as the Cowboys are set to host the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers. If Dallas really wants to win this matchup against a longtime rival, a good start would be getting healthy. The Cowboys have been hit with the injury bug , but the good news is that prior to this matchup, they're getting healthier--as several key players are off the injury report and are good to go. The Cowboys are set to get some key starters back against the 49ers DeMarvion Overshown is good to go for Week 10 Overshown produced splash plays in Weeks 7 and 8 before missing the Colts game. The Cowboys will need one or two of those against San Francisco. DaRon Bland's status is in jeopardy And given Joey Porter Jr. (who we'll get to after this) is no shoo-in to play either, this isn't exactly ideal against MVP candidate Brock Purdy. Even though Bland hasn't exactly been effective even when he's been

away.headline: NFL executive has concerning prediction for 49ers’ Christian McCaffrey
away.blurb: McCaffrey carries no game designation for Sunday’s matchup with the Dallas Cowboys. He sat out Wednesday for rest, then practiced fully Thursday and Friday. Related Articles What George Pickens’ Bizarre Answer Means for His Cowboys Return vs. 49ers Texans Hit With Major Injury Blow as 4 Key Starters Ruled Out Against Browns San Francisco 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey has scored 10 touchdowns through eight games, helping his team build a 7-1 record. One NFL executive still expects the 49ers to need more from rookie running back Kaelon Black before the season ends. The executive’s praise for Black came with a prediction about McCaffrey getting injured. “He’s an explosive runner,” an NFC executive told ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler of Black, adding that “Christian [McCaffrey] will undoubtedly get hurt at some point.” Fowler included the comment in a Friday report on the NFL’s playoff races and emerging players. The executive was not identified and did not offer a reason for the injury prediction. The 30-year-old has appeared in all eight of San Francisco’s games this season. He leads the team with 457 rushing yards and nine rushing touchdowns, adding 36 catches for 270 yards and another score. Only tight end George Kittle has more receptions for the 49ers. Kaelon Black earns work alongside Christian McCaffrey Black has already become a regular part of coach Kyle Shanahan’s offense. He has 68 carries for 303 yards and a touchdown, averaging 4.5 yards per attempt. His 133 rushing yards over the past two games include a 30-yard touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons. In last Sunday’s 38-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, Black carried 11 times for 70 yards. McCaffrey had 18 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown, along with two catches for 19 yards and another score. That gave San Francisco 138 rushing yards from its top two backs, with Black accounting for more than a third of their combined carries. The rookie also handled double-digit rushing attempts in the season opener against the Los Angeles Rams, finishing with 65 yards on 14 carries. McCaffrey’s workload remains below last season’s pace. He finished the 2025 regular season with 311 carries and 102 receptions across 17 starts, totaling 2,126 yards from scrimmage and 17 touchdowns. He won the AP Comeback Player of the Year award. Through eight games this year, McCaffrey has 138 touches for 727 yards from scrimmage. His receiving role remains far larger than Black’s, who has three catches for four yards. McCaffrey caught nine passes against Washington and six against Atlanta before San Francisco’s bye. He has scored at least one touchdown in seven straight games, including two-touchdown performances against Miami, Washington and Las Vegas. away.blurb: 49ers injury report: Deebo cleared, Trent Williams questionable – NBC Sports Bay Area & California Warriors San Francisco 49ers left tackle Trent Williams sustained a shoulder injury during Thursday's practice and is questionable for Sunday's game in Dallas. Wide receiver Mike Evans will miss his third consecutive game, but Deebo Samuel is expected to return for the 49ers on Sunday. The 49ers fully cleared Samuel to return for the team’s Week 10 game against the Dallas Cowboys. He has not played since Oct. 11, when he sustained a hamstring injury in a Week 5 win over the Seattle Seahawks. “It’s been going well,” Shanahan said. “I’m sure if this was the last game or something, he’d be able to go out there. But we’re just trying to make sure it fully heals so it doesn’t act up again. But it’s going in the right direction.” Left tackle Trent Williams is listed as questionable with a shoulder condition. Coach Kyle Shanahan said Williams injured his shoulder Thursday in practice. Linebacker Dre Greenlaw sustained a knee injury in practice Thursday, too. He is also listed as questionable. The 49ers have a bit of uncertainty at cornerback, too. Starters Renardo Green (back), Deommodore Lenoir (foot) and nickel back Upton Stout (shoulder) are listed as questionable against the Cowboys. The 49ers could also activate defensive tackle CJ West (knee) off the injured reserve list. He is listed as questionable. Rookie defensive tackle Gracen Halton went on injured reserve this week after sustaining a fractured and dislocated ankle. The 49ers acquired Allen at a time when the team has experienced an abundance of injuries at wide receiver. That list includes Evans, who left the Oct. 19 game against Washington due to Achilles tendinitis. home.blurb: The TCU product was available because the New Orleans Saints released him after he appeared in six games for the NFC South team this season. He ran for 159 yards and two touchdowns on an ugly 2.8 yards per carry in those six games. Dallas Cowboys fans may have been hoping for a more consequential move ahead of Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET NFL trade deadline, but they reportedly did make a running back addition. Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News reported the Cowboys signed Kendre Miller to its practice squad with Tyler Goodson dealing with a knee injury he suffered in Sunday's win over the Indianapolis Colts. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters Monday that Goodson will miss "multiple weeks" with the setback. The timing was less than ideal for Goodson, as he was just starting to establish himself in the running back rotation behind Javonte Williams. He finished with a season-high 12 carries for 77 yards in the win over the Colts, which marked his second time in a three-game span with double-digit carries. Yet his injury put the team in scramble mode as it attempted to find another backup for Williams. Enter Miller, whom ESPN's Todd Archer reported visited with the Cowboys on Tuesday before their decision to sign him. Miller was also an occasional threat in the Saints' passing game with nine catches on a career-high 13 targets this season. While he isn't someone who is going to carry the offense on his back, the Cowboys won't ask him to do so. Instead, he will surely be put in a role where he is expected to fill in for Williams on a handful of series throughout games to keep the starter fresher for the stretch run. Next up for Dallas is a home game against the San Francisco 49ers.

home.headline: Evans OUT, Williams and Greenlaw Questionable; Deebo Returns Ahead of Cowboys | Practice Report #SFvsDAL
home.blurb: Evans OUT, Williams and Greenlaw Questionable; Deebo Returns Ahead of Cowboys | Practice Report #SFvsDAL Skip to main content Primary nav NEWS Following Friday's practice, head coach Kyle Shanahan ruled out WR Mike Evans for Sunday's game and listed seven players as questionable, including T Trent Williams and LB Dre Greenlaw . Below is the full status report. Williams was added to the injury report after suffering a shoulder injury during Thursday's practice. The veteran tackle was limited Thursday before sitting out Friday. Greenlaw is also questionable after sustaining a knee injury on Thursday. The linebacker was limited on Thursday and Friday after a rest day on Wednesday. If unable to play, rookie LB Jaden Dugger could see an increased role after stepping up in Greenlaw's absence earlier this season. CB Renardo Green (back) and DB Deommodore Lenoir (foot) both sustained injuries during the team's Week 9 win over the Raiders. Both missed Wednesday and Thursday practices before returning to limited participation on Friday. CB Upton Stout (shoulder, neck) was limited throughout the week. All three are questionable. With those three defensive backs listed as questionable, CB Nate Hobbs could provide additional depth in the secondary if available. Hobbs is also questionable for Sunday, but practiced in full this week. The veteran remains on Injured Reserve and would need to be activated to the 53-man roster to play. The lineman recorded a sack in the team's Week 1 victory over the Los Angeles Rams in Australia. Evans has been ruled out for Sunday's game as he continues recovering from his Achilles injury. home.headline: 49ers injury report: Deebo cleared, Trent Williams questionable against Cowboys
home.blurb: 49ers injury report: Deebo cleared, Trent Williams questionable – NBC Sports Bay Area & California Warriors San Francisco 49ers left tackle Trent Williams sustained a shoulder injury during Thursday's practice and is questionable for Sunday's game in Dallas. Wide receiver Mike Evans will miss his third consecutive game, but Deebo Samuel is expected to return for the 49ers on Sunday. The 49ers fully cleared Samuel to return for the team’s Week 10 game against the Dallas Cowboys. He has not played since Oct. 11, when he sustained a hamstring injury in a Week 5 win over the Seattle Seahawks. “It’s been going well,” Shanahan said. “I’m sure if this was the last game or something, he’d be able to go out there. But we’re just trying to make sure it fully heals so it doesn’t act up again. But it’s going in the right direction.” Left tackle Trent Williams is listed as questionable with a shoulder condition. Coach Kyle Shanahan said Williams injured his shoulder Thursday in practice. Linebacker Dre Greenlaw sustained a knee injury in practice Thursday, too. He is also listed as questionable. The 49ers have a bit of uncertainty at cornerback, too. Starters Renardo Green (back), Deommodore Lenoir (foot) and nickel back Upton Stout (shoulder) are listed as questionable against the Cowboys. The 49ers could also activate defensive tackle CJ West (knee) off the injured reserve list. He is listed as questionable. Rookie defensive tackle Gracen Halton went on injured reserve this week after sustaining a fractured and dislocated ankle. By Matt Maiocco, 49ers Insider • Published November 13, 2026 • Updated on November 13, 2026 at 2:46 pm The 49ers should get a further boost at wide receiver with the addition of veteran Keenan Allen, who will make his San Francisco debut after arriving in a midweek trade from the Indianapolis Colts. “He’ll have a role,” 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said of Allen. The 49ers acquired Allen at a time when the team has experienced an abundance of injuries at wide receiver. That list includes Evans, who left the Oct. 19 game against Washington due to Achilles tendinitis. home.blurb: Mike Evans 'Real Close' to a Return? "Mike's such a dog and wants to get out there all the time. And I think it'd be hard to keep him out if this was the last game or anything like that," Shanahan explained . "But what we're trying not to do is have him come back and then be out right away. We're trying to build him up the right way, so hopefully, it can last a little bit." NFL Network's Mike Garafolo said on Nov. 8 that Evans was "questionable at best" for the Cowboys game. He also compared the injury to the Achilles tendinitis that sidelined Christian McCaffrey two seasons ago. That's a big bounce back for a player who was limited to eight games in his final season with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers because of a hamstring injury and a broken collarbone. He finished that year with 30 catches, 368 yards and three touchdowns. The 49ers have split their two games without him. They lost for the first time this season to the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7. Then they came out of the bye and beat the Las Vegas Raiders 38-17 on the strength of five second-half takeaways. Second-year wideout Jordan Watkins made one of the plays of that game with a leaping 37-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter, all with Deebo Samuel also out. Samuel was limited in practice this week with a hamstring injury. That means Brock Purdy could be missing both of his top receivers again when the 49ers take on a Cowboys defense that has given up 236 points in nine games . LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Imagn Images Week 10 in the NFL is here, and it's the first week where all the players who were dealt at the trade deadline will make their debuts with their new teams. Kirk Cousins is back with the Minnesota Vikings , the Jacksonville Jaguars traded for three new defensive players, including Jordan Davis , and the Kansas City Chiefs gave Patrick Mahomes a new wideout in Josh Downs . Which one of these additions will be most beneficial for a Super Bowl run? This Sunday, the New England Patriots and Detroit Lions will battle in Germany, the Vikings and Green Bay Packers play an important divisional matchup and the Cincinnati Bengals look to steal the AFC North lead from the Pittsburgh Steelers . Which teams should you pick in Week 10, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 11 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research New England Patriots vs. Detroit Lions (-2.5) (Munich) Dajani (Lions -2.5): It's going to take me some time to get over watching the Patriots have 45 points dropped on their face by the Packers. Drake Maye threw three interceptions, and the team could now be down its top two running backs. Rhamondre Stevenson is reportedly dealing with a knee injury, while TreVeyon Henderson experienced an " unusual medical emergency ." That leaves the Patriots with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison at running back. When it comes to the Lions, the question has never been about Jared Goff 's offense but about Kelvin Sheppard 's defense. No one is talking about it, but this unit has been better in recent weeks. In fact, over this four-game win streak, they rank second in points allowed per game (15.5) and yards allowed per game (286.3). Give me the Lions. … Prediction: Lions 28, Patriots 20 Dubin (Lions -2.5): The Patriots' rapidly thinning skill-position corps gives me some doubt that they can compete with the Lions offensively. Especially after New England's secondary was just lit up by the Packers, I can see Detroit having some passing game success here, bouncing back from a slow last two weeks through the air. And then Jahmyr Gibbs is always liable to go off. Drake Maye is capable of single-handedly carrying an offense against a bad defense, but as Dajani said, Detroit's defense has been playing better as of late. … Prediction: Lions 30, Patriots 21 Kansas City Chiefs (-3.5) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Chiefs -3.5): I initially wanted to take the points here with the Atlanta Falcons , but they just got home from Madrid and sent safety Jessie Bates III to the Jaguars at the trade deadline. The Falcons were dominated by the Bengals abroad, 34-17, meaning they have lost back-to-back games by at least 16 points. The Falcons' run defense will have to be ready for Kenneth Walker III , but I think the key to not getting caught by the hook could be Josh Downs, who the Chiefs acquired this week at the trade deadline. He's not some downfield perimeter threat, but is a slot weapon that could spark Patrick Mahomes' passing game. … Prediction: Chiefs 26, Falcons 21 Dubin (Chiefs -3.5): Atlanta has been getting clobbered on the ground lately (123 or more rushing yards allowed in four of the last five games and 200 or more twice) and is about to run into the Kenneth Walker train. The Chiefs finally added someone who can beat man coverage in Josh Downs, and while it might take him a few weeks to get fully up to speed, he should help them immediately in situational football. Plus, the Chiefs' defense has been really good against both the run and the pass. This line seems several points too low. … Prediction: Chiefs 27, Falcons 16 Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Dajani (Vikings +3.5): I don't know how much time Kirk Cousins is going to need to get acclimated to his (somewhat) new situation in Minnesota, but I bet this organization and this defense are JUICED to add him to the fold. Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz simply weren't cutting it, and Cousins has actually been playing some good ball out in Vegas. His 20 passing touchdowns rank second in the NFL, and his 260.0 passing yards per game rank eighth. Cousins also has chemistry with Justin Jefferson , whose 98.9 receiving yards per game when catching passes from Cousins are the most by a QB-WR duo all-time. This Packers passing attack has been lethal with Jordan Love playing MVP football and Christian Watson and Matthew Golden looking like prime Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle , but give me the Vikings to keep it close. … Prediction: Packers 20, Vikings 17 Dubin (Vikings +3.5): In-division rematches are typically lower scoring than the first matchup, so like Dajani, I see a fairly low-scoring game here despite the fact that the Packers' offense has been a fireworks show and the Vikings just upgraded their quarterback situation. These two defenses are playing extraordinarily well right now, and I think they'll be able to get a handle on what each offense is doing. In the end, I trust Jordan Love more than I do Kirk Cousins, so we'll take the Packers in a close, low-scoring game. … Prediction: Packers 17, Vikings 14 San Francisco 49ers (-3.5) at Dallas Cowboys Dajani ( 49ers -3.5): This is historically a great rivalry, but this year it's the Super Bowl favorite vs. a team that struggles with everyone they play. The 49ers have the most games missed due to injury this season (159), but that hasn't stopped them from starting 7-1. Brock Purdy 's offense scores touchdowns on 37.2% of its drives, which is the fifth-highest rate by any team since 2000! Last week's win against the Las Vegas Raiders showed how well-rounded the 49ers are, as they scored two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and a defensive touchdown. … Prediction: 49ers 30, Cowboys 26 Dubin (49ers -3.5): I don't care how many skill-position players the 49ers are missing or how old the ones that are actually healthy are: Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy are going to cut through this Dallas defense like a hot knife through butter. The Niners are so efficient on a per-play basis both on the ground and through the air, and the Cowboys make even bad offenses look competent. Dallas might be able to get something going on its side of the ball, especially if George Pickens returns to the lineup, but I don't expect it to be nearly enough to compete with what San Francisco does on offense. … Prediction: 49ers 34, Cowboys 23 Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals (-3.5) (SNF) Dajani (Bengals -3.5): I'll keep saying it, this may be Joe Burrow 's year to win MVP. He's accounted for 26 total touchdowns through eight games, while Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have combined for 47 receptions, 693 yards and eight touchdowns just over the last three games. The Bengals have scored 34 points in three straight games and 30 points in four straight games. The Steelers defeated the Bengals in Pittsburgh in Week 3, 30-27, but the Bengals will even the series on Sunday night. Cincy is 7-2 SU and ATS in its last nine home primetime games. … Prediction: Bengals 30, Steelers 24 Dubin (Steelers +3.5): I'm taking the Bengals to win, but I like the Steelers to keep things uncomfortably close. Pittsburgh always seems to be right in the thick of it in these division games, and the first matchup was decided by only three points. I think the scoring margin is the same here, but with slightly lower scoring, in keeping with the trend of divisional rematches. … Prediction: Bengals 23, Steelers 20 Los Angeles Chargers at Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) (MNF) Dajani ( Chargers +4.5): This is potentially the worst Monday night game of all time. A winless team that hasn't covered the spread since last year vs. a spiraling team starting a new quarterback. Jacoby Brissett is an upgrade over Joe Fagnano , but how much of an upgrade immediately? I don't have a great read on this matchup, but I'll take Jim Harbaugh to keep things close with his brother's old team. … Prediction: Ravens 20, Chargers 17 Dubin (Chargers +4.5): I don't feel good at all about predicting the Chargers to actually keep a game close, but that's what I'm going to do here. I'm not going as far as predicting that they'll get their first win, but I think they can hang in the game against Jacoby Brissett in his first start with Baltimore. The Ravens' offense should be better than it was with Joe Fagnano under center, but I'm not sure it will fully hit the ground running right away. Cincinnati has strung together four wins, all while piling up 146 total points, but doing so against some softer stop units. During this stretch, the Bengals have beaten up on defenses ranked 22nd or worse in EPA allowed per play since Week 5 . The Steelers, on the other hand, have only gotten stronger on that side of the ball. Pittsburgh took time to adapt to new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham after running Mike Tomlin's playbook forever. And Graham needed time to adjust his plans to the personnel. It is huge matchup in the AFC North, where everyone is still in contention. These two teams are currently tied at the top with twin 6-2 records. Here is my SGP for Sunday’s primetime festivities, which get underway at 8:20 pm ET on NBC. Also be sure to check out our full Steelers vs Bengals predictions . Bengals ML (-180) Over 49.5 (-108) Tee Higgins Over 75.5 receiving yards (-110) Tee Higgins to score a touchdown (+120) Parlay odds: +625 Part of the value in a Same Game Parlay, of course, is that all of its components can be correlated if you so choose. That is the entire plan here, as Cincinnati receiver Tee Higgins having a big night would obviously work well with a win by the Bengals and plenty of points being scored. Let’s break down each of the three legs. Pittsburgh prevailed 30-27 in the first head-to-head showdown on September 27, but I’m not too concerned. The Steelers have swept the Bengals in a regular-season series only once since 2019. Aaron Rodgers’ squad overachieved in the first half of this season, but the first nine weeks were hardly convincing. Cincinnati, on the other hand, was mightily impressive en route to its six victories. Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are looking unstoppable. Even the defense has become an average unit – and average means good by the Bengals’ standards on that side of the ball. I’m not willing to give more than a field goal in this AFC North rivalry matchup (or really in any game involving two teams from this division), but the Bengals should be able to win it outright. This correlates nicely with the Bengals on the money line. After all, you can be almost certain that a whole bunch of points will be scored if the game is played at Cincinnati’s pace. Pittsburgh, of course, would much rather play more of a defensive slog. The first meeting between these two teams in 2026 resulted in 57 points, obviously an encouraging sign for another over on Sunday. The Bengals have not slowed down, either. In fact, they have only been getting better and better. Burrow and company have put 31, 35, 43 and 34 points on the board in their last four outings. Although Cincy’s defense has stepped up in recent weeks, keep in mind that this is a unit that got torched for 36 points by the lowly Titans earlier this month. The Bengals also watched the Steelers churn out 7.0 yards per play in this season’s first head-to-head matchup. Cincinnati ranks dead last in the entire NFL in opponents’ yards per rush (5.0), so Pittsburgh running back Jaylen Warren can be expected to go borderline crazy in this one. He turned 17 attempts into 127 yards against Cincy earlier this year. Tee Higgins Over 75.5 receiving yards (-110) and to score a touchdown (+120) Higgins has been on a heater of late – and really this entire season. The Clemson product has caught 48 of 67 targets for 758 yards and six touchdowns. He has produced at least 148 yards in three of the last five games and has scored five touchdowns in the past three weeks. Yes – five touchdowns in the past three weeks. Burrow is playing like an MVP candidate (if not even the favorite) and Chase always demands a ton of attention from opposing defenses. Elite cornerback Jamel Dean will likely be on Chase for the most part, which means things could open up for Higgins. When these two teams faced each other back in Week 3, Higgins made six receptions on seven targets for 90 yards and one TD. picks.blurb: Bengals vs. Steelers opening odds for massive Week 10 showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football College football live updates FAA ground stop updates SEC moves Ole Miss-OU to Sunday Colorado ends Houston's CFP hopes Bengals vs. Steelers opening odds for massive Week 10 showdown Alex Frank · SB Nation Mon, November 9, 2026 at 12:05 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This is as big of a home game as it gets for the Cincinnati Bengals . It's mid-November, against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and first place in the AFC North is on the line. Both the Bengals and Steelers are 6-2 and have both won four straight games. Not to mention, these two teams have already played this season. It was in Week 3, with the Steelers winning 30-27 in Pittsburgh. Right now on FanDuel , the Bengals are 3.5-point favorites next Sunday night. The Bengals' moneyline is -200, while the Steelers' is at +168. The over/under is at 47.5. Sunday night could be an extremely physical game. It's an AFC North rivalry with sole possession of first place in the division at stake. Also, it's the Bengals and Steelers. That's all you need to know for the potential level of physicality. Pittsburgh stole the first game against the Bengals, aided by two Bengals turnovers in the fourth quarter that included Joe Burrow getting strip-sacked with the Bengals on the edge of field goal range in the final minute. The Bengals never ran an offensive play with the lead in that game, but there were some great performances from their star players. Joe Burrow was 28/37 for 282 yards and three touchdowns, Ja'Marr Chase caught nine passes for 98 yards and a touchdown, and Tee Higgins hauled in six passes for 90 yards and a touchdown. Mike Gesicki also caught a 25-yard touchdown on 4th&2 early in the fourth quarter. For the Steelers, Aaron Rodgers completed 19 of 34 passes for 292 yards and three touchdowns, while Jaylen Warren rushed for 127 yards on 17 carries. Eight different players caught a pass for the Steelers, with Darnell Washington leading the way with 67 receiving yards on three receptions. Roman Wilson, D.K. Metcalf, and Ben Skowronek each caught a touchdown for the Steelers. Rodgers currently has 1,871 passing yards and 13 touchdowns on the season, but he's also thrown six interceptions and is completing just 60.8 percent of his passes. Warren has 704 rushing yards and two touchdowns, while Washington and fellow tight end Pat Friermuth lead the Steelers with three and four touchdowns, respectively. T.J. Watt, as of Sunday night, leads the NFL with 7.5 sacks, and he also has nine tackles for loss. Cornerback Jamel Dean also has three forced fumbles. Bengals right tackle Amarius Mims held T.J. Watt off the stat sheet in that game, which bodes well going into Sunday night. The Bengals' offense scored on five of their eight drives in the first meeting in Week 3, gaining 352 yards of offense and rushing for 83 yards on 18 carries. Chase Brown rushed for 61 yards on 13 carries.

picks.headline: Bengals vs. Steelers predictions: Joe Burrow, Jaylen Warren and a 34-31 final
picks.blurb: Bengals vs. Steelers predictions: Joe Burrow, Jaylen Warren and a 34-31 final - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football College football live updates FAA ground stop updates SEC moves Ole Miss-OU to Sunday Colorado ends Houston's CFP hopes Bengals vs. Steelers predictions: Joe Burrow, Jaylen Warren and a 34-31 final (Sam Greene/The Enquirer / USA TODAY) Keegan Nickoson · Roundtable Sports Wed, November 11, 2026 at 11:53 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Joe Burrow accounts for four touchdowns for the fifth straight game Burrow is on a heater, scoring four or more touchdowns, whether throwing or running, in four straight games. In his last four games against the Steelers, Burrow has thrown 11 touchdowns and four interceptions, topping 275 yards in all four games. Interestingly, Pittsburgh is a great matchup for Burrow. The Steelers play zone coverage on 84.3% of dropbacks, according to Next Gen Stats, and Burrow is the best quarterback in the NFL against zone by completion percentage, at 74.7%. Jaylen Warren rushes for 120-plus yards Warren has become one of the league's most productive running backs this season, ranking sixth in rushing yards and first in yards per carry, at 5.9. Earlier this season against the Bengals , Warren ran for the second-most yards of his season, with 127. Two weeks ago against Cleveland, Warren topped that number with 143 yards. It was the first time all season he rushed for 100 yards in back-to-back games. The Bengals' defense has been inconsistent this season, struggling with tackling some weeks and shutting down opposing offenses and forcing takeaways in others. I think that, coming off a bye, the Steelers catch the Bengals on their back foot and feed Warren, who will have a big game. Steelers win 34-31 History is not on the Bengals' side in this matchup. After playing an overseas game, teams are 0-5 when their next game comes against a team coming off a bye. The Steelers are rested, while the Bengals are recovering from nearly a full week in Madrid. A lot is at stake in this game, with the winner taking sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Pittsburgh doesn't have much momentum, especially on offense, as its best wide receiver, DK Metcalf, has been struggling with drops lately. He has just 378 receiving yards this season and has topped 100 yards just once, with a 115-yard day against Cleveland earlier this season. Metcalf had just one catch for 4 yards on six targets against the Browns. The Steelers hit a snag at the right time, giving themselves a week to figure things out. I think the Steelers pick up a big win, halting the Bengals' momentum and getting a massive tiebreaker. Pittsburgh has done a relatively good job of keeping a cap on Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins over the last couple of seasons. Outside of Chase's massive 16-catch, 161-yard game with Joe Flacco at quarterback last season, neither has topped 100 yards in their last four meetings.

Both teams are 6-2 and the winner will take control of the division down the stretch. Here are our four bold predictions for this week's game. Jaylen Warren dominates The Bengals are No. 21 in the NFL in run defense and no running back is playing better football than Jaylen Warren. We predict Warren gets his third straight 100-yard rushing game and his fifth of the season. Warren finishes with 175 yards of offense and a touchdown. The pass rush doesn't carry the defense The Bengals have done a good job keeping Joe Burrow upright and this week they keep that up. Pittsburgh sacked Burrow once in the first matchup and we predict it's more of the same as the pass rush struggles to get anything done. Two sacks this week for the Steelers defense. DK Metcalf gets it together We are getting a little extra bold here because this season has been a nightmare for DK Metcalf. But this week, we are predicting 80+ receiving yards and a long receiving touchdown for Metcalf to quiet the critics for the week. Double-digit win for the Steelers It would be easy to say the bye week cost the Steelers their momentum but head coach Mike McCarthy is 12-5 coming out of the bye and that continues this week with Pittsburgh getting a double-digit win over the Bengals thanks to a smothering defense and dominant run game. Skowronek, who began his career with the Los Angeles Rams (2021–2023), also spent time with the Houston Texans (2024) before joining the Steelers in 2024. A solid wide receiver depth piece and special teams ace, Skowronek suffered his calf injury in Week 5 and has missed the past three games. Echols, who began his career with the New York Jets (2021–2024), joined the Steelers in 2025 free agency. An underrated contributor for Pittsburgh's defense last season, Echols suffered his hamstring injury during Week 6 and has missed the past two games. Slaughter, who began his NFL career with the Jacksonville Jaguars (2025), joined the Steelers on a reserve/future contract in January 2026. After a strong preseason and training camp, Slaughter was signed back to the active roster on October 10, but unfortunately suffered a hamstring injury in Week 7 and has missed the past game. The fact that Skowronek, Echols, and Slaughter were able to be full participants at Wednesday's practice gives them an excellent shot at returning in Week 10 for Sunday Night Football against the Bengals . Skowronek, who began his career with the Los Angeles Rams (2021–2023), also spent time with the Houston Texans (2024) before joining the Steelers in 2024. A solid wide receiver depth piece and special teams ace, Skowronek suffered his calf injury in Week 5 and has missed the past three games. Echols, who began his career with the New York Jets (2021–2024), joined the Steelers in 2025 free agency. An underrated contributor for Pittsburgh's defense last season, Echols suffered his hamstring injury during Week 6 and has missed the past two games. Slaughter, who began his NFL career with the Jacksonville Jaguars (2025), joined the Steelers on a reserve/future contract in January 2026. After a strong preseason and training camp, Slaughter was signed back to the active roster on October 10, but unfortunately suffered a hamstring injury in Week 7 and has missed the past game. Fortunately, Monday night's matchup against the Baltimore Ravens could be one of their best chances to finally get into the win column. Baltimore is dealing with major injuries, including the absence of Lamar Jackson, and will turn to newly acquired quarterback Jacoby Brissett . The Ravens are also struggling to find consistency at 4-5. Meanwhile, the Chargers are coming off another ugly loss after allowing C.J. Stroud to throw for 384 yards and five touchdowns. Could Jim Harbaugh finally get his team a victory? Here are three bold predictions for Chargers-Ravens on Monday Night Football. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Bold Prediction No. 3: Jacoby Brissett throws for 2+ touchdowns in Ravens debut Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Brissett is now a Raven, and his first start with Baltimore will come at home against the Chargers . Los Angeles has a solid defense and typically does a good job making life difficult for opposing quarterbacks. However, that certainly wasn't the case against Houston. Stroud walked all over the Chargers on Sunday, throwing for 384 yards and five touchdowns. Brissett isn't the same kind of quarterback, but he has plenty of NFL experience and should have enough weapons around him to make an impact in his first game with Baltimore. I expect at least two of his passes to find the end zone Monday night. Zay Flowers could be in line for a productive performance, which would be welcome news for fantasy managers who have been waiting for the Ravens' offense to get back on track. Bold Prediction No. 2: Keaton Mitchell scores a touchdown against his former team This is probably the boldest prediction of the three. Mitchell will face his former team for the first time since joining the Chargers, and I think he'll find a way to make his return memorable. Mitchell has one touchdown this season, and it came through the air. He's recorded 46 carries for 178 yards, averaging 3.9 yards per attempt, while adding 18 receptions for 103 yards. The Chargers have continued to rotate their running backs, making it difficult to predict which player will receive the most opportunities. However, Mitchell has shown that he can contribute as both a runner and receiver. In primetime, I expect him to get a chance near the goal line and take advantage of it. Scoring against the team that gave him his NFL opportunity would make for a pretty good Monday night story. Bold Prediction No. 1: The Chargers win their first game of the 2026 season The Chargers have a chance to win? Yes, they do. Without Lamar Jackson under center, Baltimore is a much more vulnerable opponent. The Ravens are 4-5, dealing with injuries and trying to get their season back on track. Meanwhile, the Chargers are desperate to avoid falling to 0-9. There's also an interesting storyline on the sideline. Jesse Minter , who previously served as the Chargers' defensive coordinator, will face his former boss, Jim Harbaugh, for the first time as opposing head coaches. Harbaugh's first season in Los Angeles has been a disaster, but this is an opportunity to give his team something positive. Justin Herbert needs to play much better than he did against Houston, and I expect him to respond with a more competitive performance. Baltimore still has plenty of defensive talent. Marlon Humphrey and Roquan Smith could make things difficult for Herbert, while Kyle Hamilton would be another major factor if he's healthy enough to play. This could be an ugly game, with both offenses struggling to find consistency. However, I think the Chargers finally get over the hump and leave Baltimore with a victory. Score Prediction: Chargers win 20-17, with Cameron Dicker making four field goals. Los Angeles can't go 0-17, can it? This is one of its best remaining opportunities to avoid that nightmare, and I'm picking the Chargers to take advantage. away.blurb: Chargers Injury Report: 9 players sit out 1st practice of Week 10 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Chargers Injury Report: 9 players sit out 1st practice of Week 10 The Chargers began their prep for the Ravens with a whopping 18 players listed on their Thursday injury report. Of those players, over half of them sat out with a DNP tag. That group of nine included wide receiver Ladd McConkey (back), offensive guard/tackle Branson Taylor (ankle), defensive tackle Justin Eboigbe (ankle), and cornerback Isas Waxter (ankle). Every other player was given a limited designation. That group includes tight end David Njoku and linebacker Denzel Perryman, both of whom are likely to be activated this week off of IR. Offensive guard/tackle Trey Pipkins also had his practice window activated this week, although he did miss Thursday's practice altogether for personal reasons. Following the botched trade to the Broncos, linebacker Daiyan Henley was a DNP Thursday for personal reasons. Jim Harbaugh told reporters prior to practice that Henley got back to LA from Denver late Wednesday night and his attendance on Thursday was always going to be TBD. McConkey's injury continuing to keep him out of practice is worrisome. After being completely off the final injury report before the Texans game, he never made it onto the field as sudden back spasms kept him from playing. Now, four days later, those back spasms are still enough of a problem to keep him from practicing. This is most certainly something to monitor this week. home.headline: New Lamar Jackson Rumors Update When Ravens QB Had Surgery amid Latest Injury Timeline for Return
home.blurb: Baltimore Ravens star quarterback Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this season based on when he had thumb surgery. "He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return," Minter said. "We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season." Per ESPN's Adam Schefter , Jackson's surgery happened last week so based on the estimated recovery time of six to 10 weeks, he could potentially be back on the field before the regular season ends. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said in a statement on Nov. 13 that Jackson's recovery timeline was "challenging to predict" after he underwent surgery to address a dislocated and broken right thumb. A six-week recovery would have Jackson back around Week 15 when the Ravens play the Pittsburgh Steelers. The full 10-week timeline would give him a chance to play in Week 18, also against the Steelers. In addition to his hand injury, Jackson also missed three games earlier in the year after suffering a high ankle sprain. In five games, he played just 14 full quarters and threw for 961 yards, six touchdowns and one interception while adding 144 rushing yards and another score. In the wake of Jackson's injury, the Ravens traded for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who is expected to make his first start for the team against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football in Week 10. At 4-5, Baltimore has work to do if it hopes to make the playoffs. The Ravens will likely remain cautious with Jackson's recovery, making the acquisition of Brissett a critical move as they look to snap their four-game losing streak going into Monday night.

home.headline: Ravens get devastating update on Lamar Jackson’s status
home.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens offered a clearer picture of Lamar Jackson’s recovery Friday but stopped short of setting a return date for their franchise quarterback. “Recovery timelines are challenging to predict, but injuries like this that require surgery typically take about 6-10 weeks to heal. He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return.” Jackson injured his throwing hand on Baltimore’s first offensive play against Buffalo on November 1. His right hand struck Bills pass rusher Greg Rousseau as he attempted a throw, immediately ending his return to the lineup. He had already missed three games with an ankle injury. Related Articles Kirk Cousins’ Vikings Return Comes With an Emotional Twist In a statement released by the team, head coach Jesse Minter said injuries like Jackson’s broken and dislocated thumb typically require six to 10 weeks to heal when surgery is necessary. The update leaves Baltimore preparing for an extended stretch without the two-time NFL MVP as it tries to reverse a four-game losing streak. “Lamar is doing well as he recovers from the broken and dislocated thumb injury he suffered in Week 8,” Minter said. Minter described a typical healing window rather than announcing Jackson would miss another six to 10 weeks beginning Friday. The statement did not specify a target game or establish when that recovery window began. The Ravens’ quarterback problems worsened that afternoon when Tyler Huntley suffered a toe injury in the second quarter. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano finished the Buffalo game and started the following Thursday against Jacksonville. Baltimore lost those games 36-10 and 33-10, respectively, falling to 4-5. Following the loss, the Ravens made a trade to acquire Jacoby Brissett from Arizona on November 6. The veteran is preparing to make his first Baltimore start Monday night against the Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) while learning a new offense on an accelerated schedule. “It’s definitely a crash course. No question,” Brissett said Thursday. Baltimore has scored no more than 13 points in any game during its four-game skid.
